entries.title: For Sale
entries.description: Fall 1969 Charles and Mary Moat decided to sell their Maracaibo home and approached their investment management friends John Lansdell and Quentin Brown to see if a group ownership of the property was feasible. Quentin Brown took this photo from Norm Gold’s seaplane (founder of Air West – now Harbour Air). Note the small dock – Sparse tree cover due to logging – Recent clearing of part of the BC Hydro transmission line easement – The access road location.

entries.title: The Beginning
entries.description: John Lansdell arranged for a key group of his investment clients to fly to Salt Spring Island to view the Maracaibo property. In the photo from left to right are David Garrow, Charles Moat, John Lansdell, Norm Gold and Bryan Williams – Quentin Brown took the photo. This visit led to the beginning of Maracaibo with shared ownership by many families.

entries.title: Interest in ownership
entries.description: In December 1969 John Lansdell sent a memorandum to his Marlow / Yeoman investments clients to see if there was sufficient interest in forming a investment syndicate to purchase the Maracaibo property District Lot 9. A link to the first memorandum is attached. Note the price of $7,000 to buy a share in the syndicate and the terms of the purchase. Overall purchase price was $305,000 for 160 acres, the Main House and outbuildings, three A frame cottages and a small dock. Link to Memo #90 Memo #90 Dec 11 Maracaibo Syndicate1969

entries.title: Moats agree sale to Maracaibo Syndicate
entries.description: Charles and Mary Moat sold District lot 9 to the Maracaibo Syndicate in 1970. Charles and Mary had purchased this property in 1957 and called it Maracaibo. They had a great vision for the property and set about demolishing many of the old farm buildings and the original Long Harbour House. They made improvements to the Main House including adding a tropical conservatory. They dammed the bay to create a tidal lagoon, creating a swimming and boating area safe for children. They built three A frame cottages and had plans for a marina development. They felt the property should be enjoyed by more than one family. After the sale the Moats stayed on for a couple of years to manage the property.

entries.title: Charles Moats Boat House
entries.description: The boat house was removed early in 1970. This photo was taken by Quentin Brown from Norm Golds Seaplane. (West Coast Air)

entries.title: Maracaibo Syndicate exercises option to purchase
entries.description: Maracaibo Syndicate formed and exercised option to purchase District lot 9 – 160 acres $5,000 deposit full price $305,000. Link to Memo 92: Memo 92 4 feb 1970 Exercised option to purchase

entries.title: First Members
entries.description: The First List of Members: link: First Members list april1970

entries.title: Syndicate has waiting list!
entries.description: Thanks to the hard work of Quentin Brown, David Garrow and Bryan Williams amongst others, the 50 shares in the Maracaibo Investment syndicate were fully allotted and a waiting list started. Dr David Garrow (picture) introduced 15 members to the syndicate most of them from the medical profession. Link to memo 93A Memo #93A Mracaibo Syndicate march10 1970

entries.title: First meeting of Syndicate Members.
entries.description: The first meeting of the Syndicate was at the Pillars Inn Tsawwassen. The meeting was often referred to as “the infamous meeting at the Pillars Inn”. Many members had visited the property and there was a move not to treat Maracaibo like other syndicated investments but rather to keep to develop as a personal use investment, with a goal of providing cottage sites for the owners. Bryan Williams chaired the meeting and was subsequently elected as Chairman of the Advisory Committee. Link to minutes: Memo 94a minutes Pillars Inn mtg April 1970

entries.title: Bazzards on Salt Spring
entries.description: Charles and Sally spend their first holiday on Salt Spring Island, staying at the original Harbour House Hotel. They rented a boat and explored Long Harbour, long before they had any idea of moving to Maracaibo.

entries.title: Cottage Rental Rates
entries.description: A frame rental rates for the summer of 1970 were $25 per night or $100 per week.

entries.title: Martini on the Dock
entries.description: Howard Martin visits with his boat “Martini” which takes up all of the float space. Howard then arranges for three 50 ft x 8 ft cedar log floats to be built on the Fraser River and towed to Maracaibo ready for the summer of 1971.

entries.title: Investors Replaced – Members 1971
entries.description: Second membership list- the change in ownership resulted after the Pillars Inn meeting when it became clear that development for profit was not the aim of the majority. Several of the members of the syndicate who were seeking a financial investment only decided to sell to a waiting list of prospective Members. Note: This list was used at Maracaibo’s 25th anniversary celebration to recognise the Founding Members. In 1995 31 of the Founding Members remained with 19 of them attending the celebration dinner! Link to Membership List Members list February 1971

entries.title: Cedar Log Floats
entries.description: Picture shows the 150 ft. of cedar Log floats installed to provide additional moorage for 1971 summer. (photo taken in 1977)

entries.title: Davidson Dinghies
entries.description: The first couple of Davidson dinghies were donated, one by John Lansdell. These were equipped for sailing and were used in Long Harbour. Over the next couple of years two more were purchased from Members for $100 each. Picture sailing in the Lagoon.

entries.title: The 20
entries.description: 13 ft Sangster craft with 20 hp outboard (The 20) was purchased for Members use and evening beach patrols by the managers. During the 1970’s boaters would often anchor off the beaches and light campfires. These posed a serious fire risk and needed to be monitored. Charles remembers Tom Toynbee (a rowing champion) being easily able to haul the 20 onto the dock single handed. Charles’ and Sally’s combined strength could barely manage it. The 20 did great communal service until an outboard motor fell off due to some erratic driving and Members’ use was discontinued. In 1990 the 20 was replaced by the 14 ft Kellahan and sold to Henry Boudin. Picture shows Charles at the helm in 1976.

entries.title: Moats move
entries.description: The Moat family leave their Maracaibo home for a new home in Saanich, which they built with many similarities to their Maracaibo home. Members remember Charles and Mary as being very gracious and welcoming when they visited the property. They were often willing to meet them from the ferry, loan them a car and entertain them in their home, especially Bridge players. The Christmastime picture is of Jackye, Alison and Trevor Moat standing in front of the fireplace in the lounge of the old house. It is taken from a newspaper article about Christmas on Salt Spring Island.

entries.title: Toynbees Resident Managers
entries.description: Tom Toynbee is moving back to Salt Spring to take over management of the family business, Mouats Trading Company. Being a member of the syndicate he applies to live in the house and he and Yvonne agree to provide on site management of the property. Picture shows Tom with a salmon he caught fly fishing off the Maracaibo dock.

entries.title: Resort Zoning
entries.description: Salt Spring Islands first Community Plan being developed by the Provincial Goverment – Quentin Brown applies for resort zoning (C4) which was granted for 21.7 acres to be known as the Core Area. This was granted on the basis of the three existing A frame Cottages, The existing dock and proposed additional cottage sites and recreational facilities. This C4 zoning proved to be a very valuable component of Maracaibo’s development potential.

entries.title: Drinking Water Study
entries.description: Ed Livingston – groundwater geologist prepares study of drinking water resources

entries.title: First plan for development
entries.description: Richard Mann Architect – prepares study on how the peninsla could be developed.

entries.title: Easter Egg Hunt
entries.description: Easter egg hunt tradition started by the Dr. John Price family (1972 approximately) The hunt was held in the wood behind the barn, where the new Dogwood cottage now stands.

entries.title: Name Change
entries.description: Name changed from the Maracaibo Syndicate to the Maracaibo Association. (There were rumours on Salt Spring that “The Syndicate” (mafia) had bought the peninsula)

entries.title: Agreement to Purchase District Lots 8 &10
entries.description: John Lansdell and Jack Russell negotiate an agreement for the Maracaibo Syndicate to purchase District Lots 8 and 10 from the Russell Family less 10 acres including their home “Toad Hall” which the family would retain. Sadly 10 days later Jack died of a heart attack, but the deal agreed upon was honoured by his estate in 1974.

entries.title: Land Development Freeze
entries.description: NDP government elected and 10 acre development freeze imposed on all the Gulf Islands pending formation of The Islands Trust and zoning regulations

entries.title: Teepees and Christmas Trees
entries.description: Jim Russell and friends, including Bob and Jackye Mills (Moat) and David and Donna Brown, organised the clearing of approximately one and a half acres of land under the BC Hydro right of way to plant 1,000 Christmas trees. This was the same area that would later become the powerline meadow. Assisted by grants from Hydro and Maracaibo, according to Quentin, the tree planting itself was not a resounding success, but teepees were erected on the Russell property and a lively communal time was had by all.

entries.title: Islands Trust Formed
entries.description: The Province recognizes the Gulf Islands as a unique area threatened by over-development and establishes the Islands Trust. The Islands Trust Act solidified the Province’s mandate to preserve and protect the environment and unique nature of the islands.

entries.title: Distict Lots 8 & 10 Purchased
entries.description: Settlement of the Russell Estate permitted the Maracaibo Association to proceed with purchasing District Lots 8 and 10. To raise funds to complete the purchase, 70 new units of membership in the Association were created and assigned to the Russell Estate. As a pre-condition 20 of the units would be sold for cash at $10,000 per unit. The Association further guaranteed to sell 25 units at prices escalating to $15,000 per unit over five years. The remaining 25 units would be for the Russells with no guarantee of re-sale. (photo of Migs Russell)

entries.title: Tera Report
entries.description: Helmut Urhan (environmental consultant) of TERA Environmental Resource completed a Physical and Natural Resource Inventory of the Athol Peninsula for the Maracaibo Association. This substantive report sets the parameters for how the property should be developed and was commissioned to provide guidance to Bob Hassell in preparing development options. Tera report pdf: Tera Report 1975

entries.title: Easter Storm
entries.description: Easter Monday 1975 there was a big windstorm, powerlines were down and ferries cancelled. Members staying in cottages had to stay an extra night, some bunking in with an incoming family. Pictured are Bratty, Pickering and John Price children. They may well have been part of this.

entries.title: Leaky Tiki
entries.description: Maracaibo’s Huckleberry Finn, Tom Toynbee junior, built a cabin on an old raft, added an outboard motor and would set off on adventures in Long Harbour. Often he would take visiting Members’ children with him. Andrew Farry was one of them.

entries.title: Toynbees Moving
entries.description: Maracaibo was looking for new resident managers to replace Tom and Yvonne Toynbee. Charles Bazzard, manager of CIBC in Ganges, heard about the job possibility and contacted Tom. Tom invited Charles to visit Maracaibo and he knew right away he wanted to apply. Without letting Sally see the place, knowing she would be very disappointed if they were turned down, he said he was interested. Quentin Brown came to SSI to interview them(3 hrs) and then Charles went to Vancouver to meet John Lansdell. Once Charles had the job he took Sally to see their future home.

entries.title: Bazzards House Sit
entries.description: Bazzards House sit at Maracaibo between Christmas and New years while the Toynbee’s go skiing.

entries.title: Toynbees Move On
entries.description: Toynbees leave Maracaibo to move into their new home at Southey Point (picture from left to right Charles, Sally Bazzard, Mary Moat, Yvonne and Tom Toynbee – photo taken late 1990’s)

entries.title: New Resident Managers
entries.description: Charles and Sally Bazzard move to Maracaibo as resident managers. The Bazzards were the first managers to be paid! Charles worked the first 100 hours a month to pay the monthly rent on the house and after that earned $4 per hour. Charles had to provide his own tools and truck too. To make ends meet Sally kept her full time job with the BC Assessment Authority in Ganges and Charles joins a partnership in the ownership of the Vesuvius Bay grocery store. (picture of Charles and Sally with their corgis Rufus and Bronwen)

entries.title: First Workshop
entries.description: After arriving at Maracaibo Charles’ first construction job was to close in the carport at the Main House to create a workshop for his newly acquired tools. I am telling this story now because it has an impact in a couple of years time.

entries.title: Carefree visits
entries.description: Doug Welch visited Maracaibo in his 58ft Genfell “Carefree”. This was the first boat into the dock since the Bazzards arrival. She was a beauty. Doug asked for a water taxi to take them to Ganges to buy groceries, but Charles offered to bring the groceries back from his evening shift at the Vesuvius grocery store. The Welch’s were delighted and invited Charles and Sally on board for a drink, the first of many wonderful social interractions with Members on their boats at the dock.

entries.title: Phase 1 District Lot 8
entries.description: Decision made to subdivide a portion of District lot 8. Two of these lots were for the Russells’ homestead. Bob Hassell (planner) Charles Bazzard (site manager). The initial survey found the whole of District lot 8 land area was 17 acres larger than the previous survey! The area was zoned Rural with 5 acre lot average size permitted. It was decided to maximise the density to take advantage of higher values along the waterfront which resulted in 50 acres being subdivided into 19 lots with an average density of 2.63 acres per lot. As a result Phase II of D.L. 8 would have a reduced density (16 lots on 128 acres).

entries.title: Cottage Housekeeper
entries.description: Erica Ibing is hired as housekeeper looking after the Cottages. She came with great experience having once ben Head House keeper at the Banff Springs Hotel. She worked until 1990 when, aged 80, she retired reluctantly having broken a hip. Erica was a great support to Charles and Sally, looking after Maracaibo and sometimes the children too, when they were away on holiday.

entries.title: First Olympics
entries.description: The 1976 Olympics were held in Montreal. The Williams family were spending a week in a cottage. Audrey smuggled a TV into the cottage so she could watch the games. The family were aghast and decided to organise their own Olympics as an alternative to watching TV. The Vogel and George Price family also competed. Charles Bazzard was asked to judge. Events included Runing races, long jump, high jump, swimming races and backgammon!

entries.title: Laser Club
entries.description: Quentin Brown arranged for the purchase of two Laser sailboats. A club of 20 members each donating $100 towards purchase of the boats was formed. Membership was for a life. Annual maintenace fee started at $10. Over the years Membership in the club expanded and three more boats were purchased. Laser sailing was very popular up until the early 2000’s when interest in kayaking took over. Eventually the club was disbanded and all Maracaibo Members can use the boats at no additional charge. For a number of years Laser races were part of the Maracaibo Olympics events.

entries.title: Development Proposal
entries.description: The Association hired a planning team consisting of Helmut Urhan (ecologist), Bob Hassell (design consultant) and Don Vaughan (landscape architect) to prepare a Development Proposal for the Athol Peninsula. Link to Development proposal: Development proposal 1976

entries.title: Pickleball Courts
entries.description: In 1970 Jack Russell proposed building a tennis court at a cost of between $3,500 – $5,000 but a site could not be agreed upon. The Beckmann family had a Pickle Ball court at their home in Vancouver and in 1976. Quentin Brown was easily convinced that Pickleball was a great game, that the footprint required was a quarter of the size of a tennis court and so construction was approved by the Advisory committee. Charles Bazzard designed the net posts so they could to be raised to allow badminton to be played as the courts as they are the same size. Pickleball has proved a great success over the years.

entries.title: Clamshell Cottage
entries.description: Sally Bazzard who was working for the B.C. assessment Authority advised that the property tax on District Lot 10 (250 acres) could be halved if an improvement was built on the lot. Charles designed a simple A frame cottage based on a magazine drawing. Charles Bazzard and Mike Spencer started construction in December and had the site cleared and footings poured before the end of the year. This was enough enough to Assessment Authority and save on taxes. By January the roof was being shingled and the cottage was completed ready for rental for the summer of 1977. Net cost to build and furnish after reduction of property assesments was $3,132. Photo taken in April 2017. Some of you will rember the hinged roof that lifted to provide indoor/outdoor living space.

entries.title: Dock Piling extensions
entries.description: Extreme high tides following winter storms raised concern that the docks would float over the top of the pilings. Metal hoop extensions were added as a safety precaution.

entries.title: Pip Born
entries.description: Pip was delivered at Lady Minto Hospital by Dr Peter Rowell. Now the Bazzards life took on a new dimension. Maracaibo was needing more of Charles time so he gave up his partnership in the Vesuvius Grocery store and worked full time at Maracaibo. Sally worked part time for the public nurse, but more and more her help was required to keep up with the work at Maracaibo.

entries.title: Clamshell Cottage Completed
entries.description: When Clamshell was completed, It was pretty basic. Access was by a narrow gravel road . There was no water or eletrical power. Propane was installed for lights and cooking, a wood stove for heat, and an outhouse nearby. Water had to be carried in. Hence the cottage was often called the “Wilderness Cottage”.

entries.title: Electric Power For Dock
entries.description: David Price was the first Maracaibo Members’ son hired to work at Maracaibo for the summer. In the photo David on the left. Charles and David hand dug a trench from the Laundry Room to the dock for an electrical installation. It took three very hot days. The electrician complimented us on our trench but suggested it is much easier and quicker to hire a machine to do the digging. Backfilling took a backhoe about 30 minutes! A backhoe went on the wish list.

entries.title: Sea Wall Collapse
entries.description: Seawall on west side of the Main House collapses due to high tide and erosion. A new wall had to be build very quickly to save the house footings from erosion. The next low tide we excavated and prepared forms for a wall fitting. The next day we poured the footings using a pumper truck to reach over the house, and day after the wall was poured. The weather was extremely hot and the concrete had additives to speed up curing to set ahead of the incoming tide. We had to move fast!

entries.title: Strata Development Proposal
entries.description: In 1977 the Province of B.C. was developing regulations to allow development of bare land in a similar way to as condominium ownership. This opened the door to a style of development appropriate for the Members at Maracaibo. A meeting of Members was held at the Planetarium in Vancouver. Bob Hassell led a presentation showing development options for the whole property. Some Members expressed concern that such a beautiful property should be developed. Bob took those concerns into consideration andthis led to the development of a Master Plan that was presented in 1978.

entries.title: # 4 Cottage Approved For Construction
entries.description: Dogwood Cottage approved for construction. The architect was Barry Griblin (Bob Hassell’s partner), contractor Eddy Jang, construction contract price $39,445. Claire Pickering and Graham Clay were on the building committee and very involved in choosing the furnishings. The cottage was completed in time for the 1978 summer season. This first Dogwood cottage, (also known at #4) and now removed to develop Core Area housing, was beautifully sited with a lovely outlook down Long Harbour amongst the arbutus trees. The living room with its window seats was a wonderful social space and suitable for large gatherings of family and friends.

entries.title: Cy Peck
entries.description: Jim Russell and his friend Finbar, new owners of the Cy Peck, moored her in Long Harbour in 1977. The Cy Peck had been the ferry from Swartz Bay to Fulford Harbour – carrying capacity 8 cars! Jim and Finbar were fixing her up to tow north as a fishing camp or packer. The Cy Peck was a great source of entertainment and angst for the Long Harbour residents. The paint job which was dependant an cheap supplies or donations, was pink one side and green the other! One stormy day she was careening around at her moorings and one end broke free. We managed to secure a line to a mooring bouy and she rode out the storm.

entries.title: Jim Clement
entries.description: Jim Came to work at Maracaibo for a couple of days a week to help with the workload. He worked until 1982. Jim had been a postman and was attacked by a dog and had to retire early. One of the side affects of the attack was a complete loss of smell. This proved beneficial at Maracaibo as Jim would willingly tackle smelly jobs like clearing out Mink and Otters from under the cottages and on one occasion emptying a full fridge that had been without power for several months.

entries.title: Oyster Farm
entries.description: John Price, David Garrow and Bryan Williams encouraged Charles to apply for an oyster lease. The stock of oysters on the beaches was dwindling and it was thought an oyster farm might provide extra revenue for the Association and the Bazzards. An 8 acre water lease was obtained in Long Harbour fronting what is now the core area housing site and Charles and Sally set about setting up a farm. There was much to learn. McNicholl oyster trays were purchased and stocked with oyster spat collected in Desolation Sound. Quentin Brown, whose grandfather had been in the oyster business in Whistable England, arranged for several shipments of oyster spat from Whistable. Unfortunately they didnt survive in our alien waters, but we did have success growing Pacific oysters. They were suspended in trays just below the surface where they could feed 24 hours a day. Nutients are plentiful there and the shellfish could be ready for market in as little as 18 months. Oysters growing on the beach take 5 years or more to reach market size.

entries.title: Jenny Wren
entries.description: Jenny Wren, the longest permanently moored boat at Maracaibo, arrived in 1978. The Bazzards had exchanged her for the price they could get for their Toyota Land Cruiser less the cost of buying an old 1950’s Chevy truck! A 1939 Yachting World small boat of the year winner, she may be the only surviving boat of her design. After many adventures, some quite harrowing, Jenny Wren still chugs up Long Harbour with her original Lister Air Cooled 8 hp diesel 1960’s engine or sails with her lug sail hoisted. Jenny Wren is a familiar sight and sound to many in Long Harbour.

entries.title: Lot 8 Phase I construction
entries.description: Lot 8 Phase 1 subdivision underway- Cec Bader of Discovery Land services was awarded the road building contract. Bob Hassell was the planner, Don Vaughan and Jane Redpath landscape architects. Overall management by Quentin Brown and Charles Bazzard as site manager. Pre-marketing of the lots to Members commenced with prices ranging from $25,000 to $57,000 less a 10% discount for cash.

entries.title: Maracaibo Estates Management Roll
entries.description: Maracaibo Estates took over the operation of the rental cottages and marina, and from then on bookings and payments were done through the resident managers. 1978 was still early in the development of computers so the accounting was all done in written ledgers. The “Office” was located in what had been the dining room of the Main House, and with its dark wood panelling it was not the brightest office space. The entry was through the front door so the managers often found Members or visitors wondering through the house!

entries.title: Maracaibo Estates Ltd Incorporated
entries.description: To limit liability and for tax advantages it was decided to form a company to develop District Lot 8 and Maracaibo Estates Ltd was incorporated. The Advisary Committee of the Association was appointed as Directors (Howard Martin, Migs Russell, Bryan Williams, David Garrow and John Price) – Howard Martin was elected as President and Charles Bazzard as General Manager. The Maracaibo Association continued to exist as the owner of District lots 9 and 10. The whole of District Lot 8, less acreage retained by the Russells, was sold to Maracaibo Estates Ltd for $350,000. Maracaibo Estaes Ltd did not have any capital so it was a paper transaction financed by Marlow-Yeoman. Howard Martin served on the Board for 18 years. A businessman and developer from West Vancouver, Howard played a pivotal role in getting the ball rolling to develop Maracaibo as the only practical way to attract new Members and thereby meet the financial obligations to the Russell Estate. Although Howard could be described as crusty, he was a good sport and for a number of years was the official opener of the Maracaibo Olympics having become known as King Howard. He took the role seriously and every year Joni, his wife would make him a new crown.

entries.title: Development Debate
entries.description: The debate continued through 1978 as to whether District lots 9 and 10 should be developed. John Lansdell’s memo of November 22 Master Plan describes the two camps of Members as “Developers and Conservationists”. Years later one of the main “Conservationists” said that the development had been very well done and that they were completely happy with the outcome.

entries.title: RVYC Meeting
entries.description: Dick Vogel arranged a meeting for Members to garner support for the Bare Land Strata subdivision proposal. Bob Hassell and Charles Bazzard were invited to speak. The meeting was held at the Royal Vancouver Yacht club and was well attended by the “Developers”

entries.title: First Maracaibo Truck
entries.description: Ford 3/4 ton purchased – previous truck The 1950’s Purple Chevy was sold by Charles to Andrew Farry. The ford was 4 wheel drive which was needed to negotiate the rough roads under constuction. Benches were built in the back to transport members on lot selection tours. These happened most weekends through 1980 and Charles hardly had a weekend off!

entries.title: Members Commit
entries.description: 44 members sent in letters expressing an interest in buying a lot and enclosing a loan of $10,000 each for the right to enter a lot selection draw.

entries.title: Planetarium Meeting
entries.description: Members meet at the Planetarium in Vancouver – Bryan Williams chairs a meeting – Bob Hassell presents a proposal for the Development of District lots 9 and 10 ( to become phase I of Strata Plan 905). Despite concerns about being able to maintain the ambience and natural beauty of Maracaibo the majority voted to proceed with development.

entries.title: Lot 8 Phase 1 Complete
entries.description: Lot 8 Phase 1 completed – 10 out of 17 lots sold to Members. Migs Russell sold her spare lot to Norm Gold. Prices ranged from $25,000 to $57,000 with a 10% discount for cash and a further 10% discount for Members. Proceeds allowed Maracaibo to sell extra shares and raise funds to meet its commitment to the Russells. This also provided capital for the development of Strata Plan 905 that followed soon after. Shortly after sales were completed real esate prices rocketed up with some lots re-selling for triple the price within a year, however prices soon came crashing back down in the early 80’s.

entries.title: Strata on site planning
entries.description: Development planning in high gear – Bob Hassell and Charles Bazzard staking out house sites – driveway routes – road access and septic field locations. Charles on site clerk of the works supervised by Quentin Brown from Vancouver. Cec Bader hired to construct roads and watersystem.

entries.title: Strata Development Contract
entries.description: Road clearing commenced – Cec Bader Contractor – D8 Cat driven by Gordon Bader – Rock Truck driven by Larry Bader. one day the rock truck an ex off road mining truck was driving down the hill by lot 46 when the brakes failed. Larry tried to steer up the hill but the truck careened over the bank just past lot 45 and almost landed in the sea. It took two D8 cats to retrieve the truck!

entries.title: Hobby Cat
entries.description: Howard Martin purchased a Hobycat (small catarmaran sailboat) and paid for an addition to the Barn to store it in plus the Lasers. The tractor and implements were inside the barn along with the remains of two cow stalls.

entries.title: Oyster Business
entries.description: Oyster spat was purchased from Fanny Bay having being collected in Pendrell Sound. Members help Charles and Sally sort oyster spat and place in McNicholl trays. Oysters grow at least 5 times faster in trays suspended in the first 6 ft of the sea, as they can feed 24 hours a day. We were able to buy different sizes of oysters and bring some to market within a few months. We were selling them by December.

entries.title: Development Progress
entries.description: Boundary surveys for district lots completed and the roads rough graded.

entries.title: Lot Selection Guide
entries.description: Bob Hassell with help fom Gerard Farry, Quention Brown and Charles Bazzard produced the Lot Selection and Development Guide – A price list for lots was drawn up. Prices ranged from $17,500 to $45,000. Decision made that on completion every member would receive a dividend of $7,500. (picture – Gerard Farry) link to sample Lot Sketch and Guideline and Lot Development Guide (Picture Gerard Farry)

entries.title: Kingfisher Lane Decision
entries.description: Original strata budget increased from $700,000 to $1,000,000 with the decision to build Kingfisher Lane and create waterfront rather than upland lots in that area. The Master Plan was amended accordingly.

entries.title: Lot Selection
entries.description: Lot selection procedure was set out. The first 44 Members who lent the company $10,000 each would be entered into the First draw to choose a lot. Names would be drawn out of a hat and Members could then choose a remaining lot. Members were encouraged to view the lot sites and put together a list of their choices as they would have only a few minutes to make a decision before the next name was drawn.

entries.title: New Years Eve
entries.description: Starting in 1976 the Bazzards hosted New Years in the Main House for whoever was at Maracaibo. Regulars in the 1970’s were the Brown and J Price families. Gradually as homes were built more members came until it grew so large that we had to move the bedroom furniture out (of what was later to become the Members lounge to accommodate everyone. Parties continued at the Main House until 1995 when the Bazzards were away and it was decided that with the growth in numbers it was too much to accommodate the growing numbers. 40 years from today the Bazzards are spending New Years with the First Members that joined Maracaibo in 1976 after they arrived – The Bradys!

entries.title: Erosion Control
entries.description: Erosion work along the shore in front of Dogwood Cottage and A Frames started Surplus rock blasted during road construction was placed at the base of the cliffs. The work was extended in 1990.

entries.title: Tractor Replaced
entries.description: The Old Ford Ferguson Tractor was replaced with a brand new 35 hp 4 wheel drive Kuboto tractor. A brush-cutter was also purchased. This was needed as we now had about 6 kilometers of road sides to maintain and 3 km to snowplough. The picture shows the tractor with a chipper attached being used to FireSmart in the Nose Point area.

entries.title: Wells
entries.description: A number of wells were drilled to service the new development – over the years Charles supervised the drilling f 19 wells for present and future use.

entries.title: Progress
entries.description: Development construction on time and budget and water system nearing completion. Cottage bookings at capacity as Members come over to view lot choices.

entries.title: Part Time Help
entries.description: Jim Clement worked a few days a week helping with general maintenance. A very cheerful Englishman, Jim had lost his sense of smell when knocked over by a dog when working as a postman. He would happily tackle smelly jobs at Maracaibo!

entries.title: Lot Selection Draw
entries.description: Lot selection meeting at Robson Square Media Centre. Dr John Price Chair. Sally Bazzard draws names out of a hat and member has a few minutes to choose a lot. Most members came prepared with ranked choices. The meeting proceed smoothly with all 44 members selecting a lot. The Farrys were first out of the hat and chose Strata lot 23. A few swaps were made by the end of the evening but sixteen scored their first choice. (picture Dr John Price Chairman of the Advisary committee in 1980. John was on the Committee from 1977-82 and then served again as Chairman of the Board from 1996 to 1997)

entries.title: Summer Help
entries.description: From 1980 through 1983 we had several teenagers working for us during July and August – all Members’ children. For many it was their first job. They would live and eat with Chares and Sally at the Main House, where they paid $10 a day for full board. In 1980 these staff helped with road and waterline construction and then for the next few years focus was on developing the trail network. Cottage cleaning, meadow mowing and Olympics preparation were all part of the routine. (photo Ann, Shannon and Aynsley – “Charlie’s Angels”) Hiring of Members children as summer staff continued well into the 1990’s, after that the supply dwindled and we started hiring university students

entries.title: Paving
entries.description: Decision made to pave all the roads – budget increased by $154,100. Contract awarded to Jack Cewe Paving Vancouver. Asphalt was barged to Ganges and a fleet of 26 trucks worked for two days transporting asphalt for 48 hours to pave the roads in a continuous lay! Kingfisher and Maracaibo Lanes were paved later, two trucks at a time, by ferry from Duncan.

entries.title: Backhoe purchased
entries.description: The Backhoe was purchased to help with the maintenance required for the new development. It was also used to build driveways and install waterlines. The cost of the machine was around $39,000. Maracaibo Contracting was started to offer services to members on their newly purchased lots, and we made enough revenue from contract work installing waterlines and building driveways and simple excavation work to recover the cost within a couple of years. Charles had never driven a backhoe before and the drive back from Victoria with the new machine was a challenge! A switch had been left turned off that disengaged the engine brake so driving downhill was thrilling! Chris Springford who had been working for the Baders on the road construction was hired by Maracaibo to do a lot of the initial waterline and driveways installations.

entries.title: Lot Sales Completed
entries.description: All the lots sold in Phase I of Strata Plan 905 Strata Lot Owners 1980

entries.title: Water Utility
entries.description: A water utility was formed to manage and account for the Water System and Charles had to qualify as a Small Water System Operator. The water utility required a seperate accounting and became the fourth entity that required separate book keeping – Maracaibo was getting complicated with The Maracaibo Association, Maracaibo Estates Ltd, Strata Corporation 905 and The Maracaibo Water Utility to administer. Eventually the Maracaibo Association was dissolved and rolled over to Maracaibo Estates Ltd and The Water Utility was dissolved and rolled over to the Strata. Managing the watersystem requires daily monitoring and Pete Davidson and James Sinclair are certified Small Water System operators, which require annual upgrades to maintain their standing.

entries.title: Maracaibo Burgee
entries.description: A Maracaibo burgee was designed – photo shows the burgee in the office window. A circle with the sea at the bottom, a green M representing the Island surrounded by a yellow sun. This became the official burgee of the Maracaibo Olympics and was hoisted as part of the opening ceremony.

entries.title: Cash Dividend
entries.description: Registration of lots completed and a $7,500 distribution made to all Members. Members who were purchasing a lot used the distribution to reduce their purchase price. This meant that some lots only cost a net of $10,000 to purchase. Members who purchased lots were happy and those members who opted not to purchase a lot were also happy as most of them were amongst the initial Members who had paid $7,500 to join and therefore received 100% of their investment back!

entries.title: Burgee for Boats
entries.description: A competion for a burgee for boaters was held, several desighns were submitted all somewhat similar. The winning design was by Dianne Price

entries.title: Carolling
entries.description: Christmas Eve carolling tradition started by the Bazzard family. Initially carolling happened with the Bazzards calling at the A frame Cottages, then as houses were built they were included. Eventually there were too many houses to visit. Carolling moved to the Gazebo and then to the Barn and now it is held in the Members lounge.

entries.title: Marlow Yeoman Management ends.
entries.description: John Lansdell and Quentin Brown retire and all of the management is now carried out by the Board of Directors of Maracaibo Estates Ltd and the Strata Council. Charles and Sally Bazzard take over the office management previously carried out by Marlow Yeoman / John Lansdell and Quentin Brown. John and Quentin had guided Maracaibo through its formative decade culminating in the successful development of Phase I of strata plan 905. Quentin especially was entranced by Maracaibo and worked tirelessly to ensure its success.

entries.title: Windsurfing Lessons
entries.description: Larry Roy, neighbour and high school PE teacher, offers windsurfing lessons at Maracaibo, This became very popular throughout the 1980’s and was adopted as a Maracaibo olympics event.

entries.title: Gary Brady President
entries.description: Gary Brady was elected as President taking over from Howard Martin who remained on the Board. Soon after Gary was elected Marlow Yeoman had some investment troubles. Maracaibo funds were delivered by John Lansdell to Gary Brady who worked across the street, with instructions that the cheque be banked immediately. This was done and Maracaibo’s liquidity remained secure. At the 1985 AGM Les Little thanked Gary Brady for his service “Gary has been a Director and on the Advisory Committee since 1979. During that time he was involved in the Development of Phase 1 of the Strata Development, the change in management control and the rollover from the Association to the Company, a time that has seen many improvements to the facilities at Maracaibo and that has involved a large number of meetings. I believe Gary never missed one of them!”

entries.title: Tax Free Rollover
entries.description: The Maracaibo Association was dissolved and all the assets were rolled over to the Shareholders of Maracaibo Estates Ltd (120) in a one time tax free rollover. The cost base of the shares was estblished as $9,261 as at the time of the rollover.

entries.title: Strata Corporation 905 formed
entries.description: Maracaibo Estates as developer handed over the management of Strata Plan 905 to the newly formed Strata Corporation 905. Maracaibo was amongst the first Bare land Strata Developments to be registered. The following lot owners were elected to the Strata Council – Gary Brady (Chairman), Howard Martin, Bryan Williams, John Price, Claire Pickering. The same members were elected to the Board of Directors of Maracaibo Estates Ltd. plus Joe Weiler and Howard Pendleton. The First Annual General Meeting of the Strata Corpration and Maracaibo Estates Ltd was held at the Arbutus Club in Vancouver.

entries.title: Tennis Courts
entries.description: After much discussion about a suitable site a tennis court consultant was hired. Debate continued – should there be a tennis membership fee like the laser club? (do you remember “anyone for Dennis”?) Eventually the courts were constructed and tennis was very popular through to about 2010 after which the number of active players has slowly declined. In order to increase cottage booking an annual tournament was started in 1986. This was a two day event with lunch catered at the courts and a dinner on Saturday night. For many years the highlight was a lamb BBQ held in the lounge at the Main House. This was a very popular and fun event spanning about 30 years.

entries.title: Annual Dues and Fees
entries.description: Annual Dues were introduced in 1973 at $25, $35 in 1974 and $50 a year from 1975 to 1978. In 1978 dues increased to $100, but in 1980 and 1981 no dues were charged because of the development income. In 1982 Maracaibo Dues were $200 and Strata Fees $255.12

entries.title: Strata Phase II Start
entries.description: The strata subdivision application for approval was made for a two phase Development – Phase 1 for lots 1-72 and phase II for lots 73 to 86. A condition of the approval was commencing with the second phase within a limited time frame. It was decided to clear the road right of way for Phase II as timber values were good and we were able to recover the clearing costs and road rough=in from the proceeds of selling logs. Members were canvassed to see if there was enough interest in proceeding with the second phase of development. There was little interest so the project stayed on hold until 1990.

entries.title: Dock Walkway
entries.description: Wooden walkway to dock was in dire need of replacement and raising as it submerged during high tides and the support logs were rotting!

entries.title: New Dock Walkway
entries.description: Installing the new Aluminum Walkway – Charles helped by Eddy Jang’s house building crew. Large yellow cedar blocks were inslled to raise the height of the walkway. Demand for dock space during July and August is very high so 100 x 8 ft Topper Float was purchased and towed over from the Fraser River in time for the 1982 season.

entries.title: Olympics 82
entries.description: Growing in popularity every year the events always end with a Salmon BBQ and Potluck,with medals for the team captains and balloons for the younger children. Photo Patty Vogel about to hand out balloons.

entries.title: Larry Field
entries.description: Larry Field came to work at Maracaibo to replace Jim Clement. Larry worked two days a week and was a great help. He owned what is now known as the Oaks Spring Strata and he developed that property. Larry and his wife Cathy built the log farmhouse so he had good practical skills.

entries.title: The Rutter
entries.description: Maracaibo owned two boats (the “20” and the “9.9” which referred to horsepower) which the members could use for the price of fuel. They were very popular but expensive to maintain and after some shenanigans in the harbour resulting in the outboard motor falling off it was decided that useage should be modified. The 9.9 was sold and the 20 reserved for staff use only. A 16 ft boat “The Rutter” was purchased for rent to members. This had an inboard diesel engine and was very slow in comparison to the previous boats, but was quite popular with a rental rate of $5 per hour. After a few years however it was decided Maracaibo should get out of the motorboat rental business.

entries.title: Water Tower Conversion
entries.description: The water tower, reminiscent of a log fort, was built in the early 30’s to provide water pressure in the house. By 1970 the tower had quite a lean, like the one in Italy. It was jacked up to staighten it and proper foundations installed. It was also decided to expand the building to add washrooms and an out-door shower. Eddy Jang was contracted to do the work. designed by Charles with help from Bob Hassell.

entries.title: Oyster Business Sold
entries.description: Maracaibo is very busy and the income from the oyster business does not justify the time spent on the operation. At the height of the business we were selling 60 dozen oysters a week but to expand we were required to build a packing plant, a ridiculous requirement as we only sold live oysters in the shell. We sold oysters to Neptune Foods in Victoria, Coopers Cove Oyster Farm in Sooke, at the Farmers Market in Ganges and to the Harbour House Hotel. All the stock and equipment were sold to an oyster farm setting up on Saturna Island. It was an interesting venture, we grew excellent oysters fast, but the marine fouling (barnacles especially) was very heavy and providing clean oysters for the restaurant market was very labour intensive. We managed to clear our costs but did not get adequate reward for time. We also experimented with growing mussels in mesh ‘socks’ suspended from a raft. Charles collected mussels from rocks in Active Pass and they grew very succesfully until the ducks and otters found them!

entries.title: Flooding
entries.description: A major winter storm with a south easter blowing for more than three days combined with very high tides resulted in flooding of the Main House. The carpet in the downstairs bedroom was washed by the seawater and Pip was keen to go fishing from the window! There were many years that the tide would flood over the banks, but 1982 was the highest. The sea flooded right across the road to level with the swimming lagoon leaving driftwood and debris scattered all over the meadows and resulting in a huge cleanup job. (picture from the den window of the Main House).

entries.title: Strata Lot Owners list
entries.description: By January 1983 a few speculators had resold their strata lots. Strata Lot Owners 1983

entries.title: Bob Hassell and the Nose Point Yacht Club
entries.description: Bob Hassell in his newly commissioned yacht “Amaryllis” set sail for New Zealand. While in San Diego Bob wanted to use the facilities of the local yacht club, but without being a member of a yacht club with visiting privileges, this was not possible. Bob called Charles Bazzard and advised him that he was now the Commodore of the newly formed Nose Point Yacht Club and that he, Bob, was the secretary – just in case anyone from San Diego contacted Charles. Bob designed and made a burgee, printed up membership cards and with no trouble gained access to the excellent facilities of a San Diego yacht club. (Photo Nose Point Yacht Club Burgee)

entries.title: Clamshell Cottage Improved
entries.description: The roof section that lifted at Clamshell was permanently raised with a new wall and sliding glass door installed, with the addition of running water and a toilet and sink, Electricity was hooked up in 1984 allowing electric light, a fridge, stove and small hot water tank. Clamshell is becoming very popular.

entries.title: Rainy Spring
entries.description: May and June were very wet and we were unable to cut the grass on the meadows. By the time it was dry enough the grass was tall enough to make hay! We hired a farm contractor who cut and baled over 100 bales.

entries.title: Trespassing and Speeding
entries.description: The newly paved roads as Maracaibo and the relative isolation of the area proved a major attraction for the local teenagers to speed and party on weekend nights. Being a private road the police did not venture onto the property unless requested. To combat the problem we installed a gate and locked it at night. This proved very unpopular with the one or two residents, who would thow away the padlock. Eventually the gate was abandoned. Speeding continued to be a problem so a number of speed bumps were installed. These too proved very unpopular and after several years were removed.

entries.title: Summer Students
entries.description: By popular demand 19 students were employed (and fed!) over the summer of 1983, some for just a week. Building trails and docks was the main focus of new work that summer. It was great fun but hard work for the caterer. The number was reduced somewhat for 1984!

entries.title: Maracaibo Olympics 1983
entries.description: The Olympics is now a well established tradition, Tennis become a popular event with the parents. After a few years the tennis became so intense that it was removed from the Olympics so that the parents could refocus on their children! Windsurfing has become very popular too. The teenagers spend their days sunbathing in the meadow waiting for a good southeaster so that they can get out on their boards. (picture shows spectators at the Olympics watching the windsurfing event). Holding the megaphone is Dick Vogel – Admiral in charge of water events. Bryan Williams was the General in charge of land events and Les Little was the Air Marshall in charge of aerial events.

entries.title: House Construction
entries.description: By the end of 1983 twelve houses complete or under construction in the Strata Development.

entries.title: Homes
entries.description: The Following Strata Lots had homes complete or under construction. 4,10,20,25,26,32.39,47,51,56,58,60,66,69.

entries.title: Thomas the Engine
entries.description: We cleaned and repaired the water tank at the entrance which was still in use, but subject to leaks at the rusty bottom. After repainting the tank green Alison Moat did a lovely job of painting Thomas the Tank Engine at the front. The far end of the tank had an overflow pipe hanging down and with a bit of creatiivity it became` a cows tail. The kids enjoyed seeing the friendly face at the entry to Maracaibo.

entries.title: Seawall
entries.description: A seawall was built between the boat launch ramp and the dock. We transported large rocks from the hydro right of way and hired a team of stone masons, headed by Andrew Curry, to do the job. Andrew had been bought over from Scotland to do the stonework at the Hastings House Hotelrenovations. A true craftsmen he trained and influenced most of the masons on the Island. During the construction Charles recalls the following incident. “I had carried a partiularly large rock in the front bucket of the backhoe to the site of the sea wall but needed to lift it into place with the back bucket. The rock was so heavy that as I lifted it the front wheels of the machine came off the ground and I was unable to steer. In order to counter balance the rock Andrew and his crew, including a huge man called Billy Two Feathers, climbed into the front bucket. I was now able to manaoever. On approaching the seawall, we found the wheelbarrow in the way. Billy Two feathers hopped out of the front bucket to move the barrow, but the lack of his weight caused the front bucket to lift again! The back went down and the tongs holding the rock released. The front bucket was now heavier than the back so descended at great speed. Luckily no one was injured and a good laugh had by all!

entries.title: Moorage Added
entries.description: Demand for moorage space continues and as more houses are built the demand for annual use justifies further expansion. To control costs the staff build the floats on the beach. Timing is criitical to get the basic framework together between tides.

entries.title: Brochure
entries.description: Alison Moat, Charles and Mary Moat’ daughter, worked at Maracaibo for the summer and designed and drew the first brochure about Maracaibo . Brochure 1984

entries.title: Olympics
entries.description: Nose Point Relay started. Commencing at the Nose Point Road turnaround each team had a runner with a baton to pass on to their team members. There were about 10 legs to the race.

entries.title: Christmas tree lease
entries.description: For a number of years local farmer Ted Akerman had an arrangement to prune and cut Christmas trees on the Hydro powerline at Maracaibo. Part of the arrangement was that Members could tag and cut a tree for free. Ted sold the trees to the Boy Scouts. When Ted decided to discontinue his lease from Hydro, Maracaibo took over, adding pruning fir trees to its many activities. Members loved being able to find and cut a tree at Maracaibo and several would make a special trip over from Vancouver. Unfortunately after a few years BC Hydro became too demanding in the amount of clearing they required, so the lease lapsed and gradually good trees became hard to find.

entries.title: Road Collapse
entries.description: One winters night, after several days of heavy rain, a girlfriend of Jim Russell’s returning late at night, suddenly noticed a hole in the road and swerved. She swore two wheels were in the air but made it safely across. Liquified by an underground stream a large chunk of Mansell Road in the Lot 8 development had collapsed. Charles spent most of the night at the scene setting up barriers and lanterns. Luckily no one was injured and the Department of Highways fixed the road and installed an extra large culvert.

entries.title: Bob Hassell returns from the South Seas
entries.description: Bob returns from his sailing adventures and Charles accompanies him on the last leg from Maracaibo to Vancouver. It had been a huge adventure. It does not take Bob long to decide he wants to live at Maracaibo and he returns, living on his boat and in Clamshell Cottage while he designs his home and office.

entries.title: Phase II strata extension of Development.
entries.description: The conditions of the approval of Phase I of the strata development required that Phase II be completed by September 1986. Due to the recession there was no interest from Members in buying lots so an extension was applied for and granted allowing another 4 years.

entries.title: Laser and breakwater dock
entries.description: A new outer float was constructed to act as a breakwater, and with a section for storing the Laser sailboats which are very popular.

entries.title: Special Assessment
entries.description: Due to the decision not to proceed with Phase II of the Strata Development it was agreed (but not without considerable debate!) that funds be set aside to allow for asset replacement. The Special Assessment was set at $100 for 1985. No further Special Assessment for asset replacement was made until 1992.

entries.title: Recreation room
entries.description: The idea of a recreation room/building for our young people to be sited above the volleyball court was discussed at the AGM but the proposal was narrowly defeated. As an alternative a fire pit was costructed at considerably less expense. This proved very popular but did cause some sleep deprivation for the managers.

entries.title: Rental Cottages
entries.description: A number of improvements were carried out to upgrade the furnishings and carpeting in the cottages. Off season mid week rental rates were reduced to encourage more rentals. Do you remember how the Cottages were furnished in the 1970’s?

entries.title: ME President – Don Graham.
entries.description: Don and family had moved from “back east” and fell in love with Maracaibo. The Grahams purchased lot 26 and Bob Hassell designed a home for them. During Don’s time as President he arranged a workshop with a professional facilitator to look at Maracaibo, what it means to its Members, and their families many of whom also took part, and to gauge their values and hopes for the future. This workshop helped reinforce the philosophies of the Maracaibo Development. Don also took a great interest in Maracaibo’s accounting systems. Up until then we had handwritten ledgers and the accounting to be put onto computer at Smythe Ratcliffe. Initially this was by completion of data sheets, but soon Maracaibo purchased its first computer and the basic accounting was completed on site. Don also introduced depreciation allowances to the accounting procedures, helping to pave the way for future capital replacements. Don also helped develop the policies on members’ families visiting priveleges.

entries.title: Trails
entries.description: For the summers 1981 through 1985, a major focus of work for our student helpers was developing new trails throughout the property. Prior to that there were very limited trails mostly following old logging roads (the Peninsula had been logged 3 times in different areas). Many of the new trail followed both logging and deer trails. It was an exciting time finding new areas on the property. Charles led a group of Sea Scouts to search for a cave we had heard about in the rainforest area. There was no trail built yet, and there was great excitement when one of the scouts found it!

entries.title: Maracaibo Olympics 85
entries.description: Tennis proves too much of a distraction for the adults (they are just too competitive). The event is dropped from the Olympics with a different weekend to be dedicated to tennis. After the Salmon BBQ a Celtic band played music at the barn for Members to dance to.

entries.title: Expo 86
entries.description: Member Richard Blagbourne was very much involved in design work for Expo 86. There was a lot of excitement throughout the Province and it was a great success. Maracaibo arranged group purchases of 3 day and season passes for Expo 86.

entries.title: C4 Zoning
entries.description: 1984/85 – Islands Trust endeavors to restrict the use of C4 zones by reducing densities and applying maximum sizes to buildings. Their main fear was that rental buildings would be turned into condominium units and sold, adversely affecting the aims of the Community Plan. The Trust proposal was so restrictive it was not approved by the Minister of Municipal affairs, but the writing was on the wall that C4 zones were targeted for downzoning. This would affect the Core Area.

entries.title: Strata Lot Foreclosure
entries.description: The local credit union foreclosed on a strata lot and wanted to market it with a bundle of other properties that had been foreclosed upon on Salt Spring. Given Maracaibo’s membership approval requirements this situation raised considerable concern. After finding a purchaser for this lot from amongst the Members we approached the credit union to attempt to buy the lot back. They were very reluctant thinking the value of the Maracaibo lot would improve their chances of selling some less desirable lots in the bundle. Negotiations escalated, involving our president and the president of the credit union, but finally agreement was reached and Maracaibo was able to buy the lot at cost.

entries.title: Snow
entries.description: Over several days in November we accumulated two feet of snow turning Maracaibo into a Winter Wonderland. The Bazzards note: ” Between snowploughing, gravelling the road, maintain pipes from freezing and office work, we enjoyed tobogganing, and cross country skiing at Nose Point.” Dick Newman of Fishermans Island told us of watching the otters build a snow slide and play for hours as they raced up the bank to slide back down into the sea.

entries.title: New Years party
entries.description: 63 Members and family came to the Main House for a New years party despite 15 inches of snow on the ground!

entries.title: #1 Cottage Fire
entries.description: Charles and Sally were called at midnight February 2nd by a neighbour from across Long Harbour who spotted #1 Cottage on fire. The bedroom was lit up by the reflection from the fire. After calling the fire department Charles went to the scene, but the cottage was fully engulfed in flame and all that could be done was wet down the cedar roof of #2 cottage to stop the fire spreading. As the building collapsed the fire department encouraged Charles to push (with the backhoe) parts of the structure that had fallen outwards into the blaze as the building was beyond any form of salvage. It was a traumatic night. The next morning our good friend Eddy Jang called by, reassuring us that he could have a crew available to build a new cottage in time for the summer season.

entries.title: #1 Cottage Fire
entries.description: Charles and Sally were called at midnight February 2nd by a neighbour from across Long Harbour who spotted #1 Cottage on fire. The bedroom was lit up by the reflection from the fire. After calling the fire department Charles went to the scene, but the cottage was fully engulfed in flame and all that could be done was wet down the cedar roof of #2 cottage to stop the fire spreading. As the building collapsed the fire department encouraged Charles to push (with the backhoe) parts of the structure that had fallen outwards into the blaze as the building was beyond any form of salvage. It was a traumatic night. The next morning our good friend Eddy Jang called by, reassuring us that he could have a crew available to build a new cottage in time for the summer season.

entries.title: Junior Members – discussion
entries.description: in 1986 there were about 150 members’ children under 25, and about 60 over 25. The concept of Junior Memberships was discussed and suggestions sought. How could share sales be structured to maximise the potential of what is seen as the best future market for Maracaibo shares? Eventually Members children over 19 were granted visiting priveleges without their parents being present.

entries.title: First Tennis tournament
entries.description: The charge for the weekend for tennis players was $65 per head and included continental breakfast Saturday and Sunday, buffet lunch at the courts on Saturday, Lamb BBQ including salads and dessert Saturday night at the Main House and brunch at the Bay Window on Booth Canal at 1.00pm on Sunday. The weekend was a great success and was the start of many similar events that lasted for 30 more years! The winners of the first tournament were Louise Quart and Glen Whitelaw. The Beckmann’s and Whites were the organisers

entries.title: Re-roofing the Main House
entries.description: We replaced the pink ashphalt roof of the main house and found that it had been laid over the original beautiful old growth cedar shakes installed for Fred Abbott in the 1920’s. 24″ with 1″ butts, tight grain. These would cost a fortune now!

entries.title: The Anchor
entries.description: Dick Vogel called Charles and said he had been given an anchor by the Admiral at Esquimalt Naval Base which he thought would look great at the entrance to Mariners Lane. All Charles had to do was pick it up. The sailing ship anchor circa 1860 was dredged up in the harbour and weighed a couple of tons plus some chain that felt like another ton. A crane, a flatdeck truck and an excavator were needed for the move. Dick was right – the anchor looks great! A few years later Dick found a bouy at Capital Iron. Charles set off to pick it up with the 1 ton truck. The bottom of the bouy is filled with concrete, so when it was first placed in the truck with the heaviest end at the back, the front wheels ifted off the ground. When it was turned around the front wheels stayed on the ground but the steering was very light going up hill!

entries.title: Focus Groups
entries.description: Don Graham, President hosted a two day focus group meeting to discuss the future of Maracaibo and how Members children could participate as future users and owners of the property. This meeting resulted in many useage changes to the policies, and in 2020 the Directors are still discussing share ownership and visiting rights. In February 1987 the Temporary Membership fee for Members children over 25 was dropped.

entries.title: Security Systems
entries.description: House security was becoming a concern and arrangements were made for Charles to install alarm systems in Members homes. These were connected to sirens in the house and by phone to the Managers. It was relatively early days in the technology of movement detection and there was many a spider walking over a sensor that would set off an alarm! However thay did prove effective in scaring off and detecting intruders. Real alarms were rare but once a door had been broken open by an axe and another where the intruder entered a house and was discovered by Charles. The police eventually caught him with the aid of a dog! The Alarm monitoring was eventually taken over by FXR.

entries.title: Tennis 87
entries.description: 32 players and 50 for dinner at the main house. This event is very popular!

entries.title: Mount Maxwell Hike
entries.description: Charles led a group of 20 Members on a hike up Mount Maxwell. Sally led a smaller group to explore the newly developed Willow Pond trail linking with Big Bluff trail. In the evening we had a potluck supper beside the lagoon.

entries.title: Maracaibo Seashore Exploration
entries.description: Charles and Virginia Campbell led a beach walk to explore the various intertidal zones at a very low tide.

entries.title: Fire on Clamshell Island
entries.description: Some kids from RVYC accidently started a fire on Clamshell Island. It quickly got out of control and Maracaibo staff responded by boat taking a portable fire pump. When the Fire Department arrived we took them out by boat and they took over using our equipment as their pump would not start! Luckily the damage was limited and the vegetation soon recovered.

entries.title: Olympics 87
entries.description: Instead of a Marathon a new event – the Triathalon was introduced. This was very exciting to watch. King Howard officially opened the games, a tradition that lasted several years. After 13 years of being the official flame lighter Anne Little passed the torch to Pip Bazzard in a joint ceremony that involved sailing accroos the lagoon with a winsurfer with Pip holding a lit bullrush! There were 140 competitors for the balloon toss.

entries.title: Trivia 1987
entries.description: The Rafts in the Swimming Lagoon were replaced. The Rutter motorboat was sold and Maracaibo no longer has motorboats for Members use. Jamie Little caught so many fish we built our first fish filleting table on the dock. The two big trees by the dock were identified – the one closest to the dock walkway is a Lebanese Cedar and the other is a Blue Atlas Cedar.

entries.title: Eddy Jang
entries.description: Eddy worked part time, still managing his contracting company at a reduced level. He had worked at Maracaibo in the mid 1960’s building the A frame Cottages and later became a general contractor and built Dogwood Cottage. During the early 1980’s his company built 12 of the houses in the strata development. In 1987, fed up with the pressure of building new homes, he asked for a part time job at Maracaibo. Eddy would cheerfully tackle any task, and was the driving force behind building, as economically as possible, the workshop and storage buildings in the works yard, straightening and expanding the water tower to add washrooms. Constructing Dogwood Cottage and the new Arbutus Cottage, the Gazebo, renovating the Barn and creating the Members Lounge in the Main House, multiple dock expansions, the boat ramp and boat grid were all achieved with Eddy’s remarkable ingenuity.

entries.title: Core Area Zoning Planning
entries.description: The Islands Trust ask Maracaibo to develop suggestions of what it would favour for a specific zoning change to the Core Area that would meet Maracaibo’s forseeable needs. The Trust had concerns that our C4 Zoning had potential for overdevelopment. A number of planning options are developed by Bob Hassell for consideration by the Members. These all entail retention of rights to develop more rental cottages but at a much lower density in return for the right to develop a limited number of house sites that could be sold and not limited to transient accomodation.

entries.title: Clamshell Driveway
entries.description: Driveway is extended to loop back to Nose Point Road and a parking area created.

entries.title: AGM – Core Area Zoning
entries.description: Held at Arbutus Club – Members approve rezoning proposal for Strata Lot 72 from C4 To a Comprehensive Development zone unique to Maracaibo’s needs.

entries.title: Trivia
entries.description: Harry White and Susan Blagborne won the tennis tournament. The K&R Grocery Store moved uptown Ganges and became the Village Market. Lots of complaints about speeding in Maracaibo. Mansell road was chip sealed!

entries.title: Canoes
entries.description: 2 canoes were purchased for the Boat Club and were a very popular addition.

entries.title: President – Bob Quart
entries.description: Don Graham stepped down as President and Bob Quart was elected. Bob served in that role until 1992. During Bob’s term there were a number of highlights, including the succesful development and sale of Phase II of the strata plan. Drilling of new wells. A review of the managers remuneration, which resulted in much happier managers

entries.title: Docks
entries.description: 240 ft additional moorage floats added

entries.title: Cottage Cleaning Day
entries.description: The Dymonds had the great idea of changing cottage changeover day in the summer from Saturday to Friday. This meant Members had a full weekend instead of two partial weekends and the staff would not have to work on a Saturday. Hard to believe we went that many years without thinking of making that change!

entries.title: Petition against private docks
entries.description: The Strata Council received a petition signed by several Members objecting to the approval of private docks fronting the common land. As a result it was agreed that existing docks could remain as long as they were shared facilities available to adjoining lot owners.

entries.title: Membership Waiting list
entries.description: It was noted that there was a long list of prospective members.

entries.title: Phase II Strata Plan 905 approved to proceed
entries.description: Decision made to proceed with Phase II strata development. 14 lots developed – 9 members loaned $40,000 each for right to draw their names from a hat to choose a lot. By 1990 development completed and all lots sold.

entries.title: Core Area Zoning change
entries.description: After much negotiation and a public hearing the Islands Trust approved a change of zoning for the Core Area (strata lot 72) to change from C4 to CD6. This unique ruling improved the practical forseeable use that Maracaibo could utilize. See pdf copy of zoning link CD 6 Zoning Maracaibo1988

entries.title: Freezing Windy Weather
entries.description: Exerpt from Newsletter #30 – We had some incredible storms this winter with very high winds, one of which bought down the flagpole, and another one with minus 12 degree temperatures and high winds which left many frozen water pipes. The road conditions on Salt Spring were appalling, as first we had sleet which froze to solid ice as temperatures dropped followed by another 3 inches of snow. The sea breaking on the docks was turned to ice and had to be cleared for fear they would sink with the weight. One good aspect of the heavy freeze was that children were able to skate on the new pond on Rain Forest Road. Snow ploughing at that time was done on the open tractor and sanding from the back of the pickup truck when we spread gravel via a shovel. Members would often lend a hand.

entries.title: Directors meeting Phase II Prices
entries.description: For the first time a Directors Meeting was held at Maracaibo. Charles led a tour of Phase II. The Directors agreed that they should hold at least one meeting a year at Maracaibo rather than in Vancouver. Photo of offering prices for lots in Phase II.

entries.title: Extraordinary AGM
entries.description: A meeting was held and a motion approved to increase the Share Capital of Maracaibo Estates Ltd to 150 shares. This was to allow new shares to be issued to purchasers of shares in Phase II of the Strata. It was agreed that shares would not be issued by the company for less than $15,000. Recent share sales had been for $14,000.

entries.title: Ist Maracaibo Wedding
entries.description: Alison Moat married Angus Graeme. It was the first wedding at Maracaibo and of particular importance as Alison had grown up and lived at Maracaibo until 1971. There have been several marriages of Members’ children at Maracaibo since then.

entries.title: Water system smelly water
entries.description: A problem developed with the water quality from the well in the worksyard. The water was smelly and had traces of hydrocarbons. It was a complicated issue, the well being located in a shale bed with bacteria producing hydrocarbons from the ancient vegetation making up the shale. Another complication was a fuel spill in the worksyard and a high level of methane gas. Eventually the problem was solved by letting the well rest and then pumping to waste and using the water for irrigation. Some 30 years later the well is clear and back in use.

entries.title: Seaplanes
entries.description: Bob Quart organises a Friday evening seaplane service direct to the Maracaibo dock for the summer months. The plane charter proves very popular and was referred to as “the daddy plane”

entries.title: Phase II Construction
entries.description: Work on the road and water system is almost complete. 13 of the 14 lots have been reserved pending legal registration.

entries.title: Mrs Ibing Retires
entries.description: Mrs Ibing who had been our cottage housekeeper at Maracaibo for 15 years fell and broke her hip. At age 79 Mrs Ibing was still able to clean a cottage faster than anyone else. For Sally and Charles she was the most loyal dependable employee and friend anyone could hope to find.

entries.title: Trivia
entries.description: 28 homes have been completed in Phase I. Three lots are offered for resale in Phase I. Islands Trust try to change Salt Spring Island community plan zoning that will have a major impact on house siting at Maracaibo – Maracaibo objects and takes legal counsel – Trust back down.

entries.title: Olympics 1990
entries.description: For the first time a theme was adopted for the Olympics – a marine event with laser and windsurfer sails providing a backdrop to the BBQ,

entries.title: A Frame Cottage Improvements
entries.description: New seaside decks – twice the size, new double glazed windows and sliding glass doors, fireplaces in alcoves, drywalled ceilings with soundproofing, and skylights in the living area and stairway.

entries.title: AGM 1990
entries.description: Request received that AGM be held on Salt Spring – It was agreed that a pre AGM meeting would be held on Salt Spring, but as the majority of Members were based in Vancouver the AGM would continue to be held at the Arbutus Club. Annual Dues are $475, Strata Fees $340, Water Rates $100

entries.title: Phase II
entries.description: Sales of all 14 lots agreed and 12 completed. Gross revenue $902,000 – cost of development $312,000. 8 new shares issued at $15,000 each generating $120,000 new capital

entries.title: Cablevision
entries.description: Installation of Cablevision explored. Various alternatives considered. Large satellite dishes deemed ugly and banned. Some Members thought Cablevision would be obsolete in the near future as satellite technology was advancing rapidly.

entries.title: Anno Delaney
entries.description: Anno takes over the duties of Mrs. Ibing, but also a variety of other jobs, including monitoring the water system, office backup and grounds and building maintenance. Anno worked a minimum of 4 days a week until she retired in 2013. Maracaibo was lucky to have found an excellent replacement for Mrs. Ibing.

entries.title: Killer Whales
entries.description: The Dymonds writer the following ” May 1990 long Harbour was visited by a pod of Killer Whales. We first heard a splash from inside or home on Kingfisher Lane. When we went on the deck to investigate we saw a number of seals along the shoreline, trying to get out of the water. Then we saw why. Directly across from us were several Killer whales. For a period of about 20 minutes they frolicked in front of us, doing the sort of routine you see at the Vancouver aquarium – breaching, tail lobbing, and spiralling clear out of the water. The ferry arrived during this time and waited while passengers surged to the decks to watch. We were told the whales had not been seen in Long Harbour for about 20 years.” Note picture of whales is in Ganges Harbour

entries.title: Simon Jang
entries.description: Simon Jang starts working at Maracaibo. Maracaibo hires the O’Donnell brothers to fall and mill some trees in District lot 8 so that we can utilize some of our own timber for building projects. Simon’s first project was building a sander and fuel shed in the works yard. He joined his dad Eddy, Charles and summer staff building the workshop and storage sheds from lumber milled on the property by Russell Hardy. Simon returned for several summers in between his time at university.

entries.title: Lots for Sale
entries.description: For the first time there are no lots listed for resale!

entries.title: Docks
entries.description: 100 ft outer breakwater replaced and Laser dock incorporated.

entries.title: Boat storage yard
entries.description: This facility was developed in 1990 after the completion of Phase II as a place to keep boats and trailers away from private lots.

entries.title: 1 ton Truck
entries.description: 1990 Chevy 1 ton truck with snowplough and sander purchased! Charles is very happy – no more snowploughing from an open tractor and shoveling gravel from the back of the pickup truck

entries.title: Indoor Swimming Pool
entries.description: Requests for an indoor heated pool were considered, but did not gain support from the majority of Members

entries.title: GST
entries.description: Invoices from Maracaibo Estates Ltd are subject to GST. Strata Corp. is considered exempt.

entries.title: Heritage Fund / Contingency and Development Fund
entries.description: It was decided that $600,000 of the net proceeds of the development of Phase II should be placed in an investment fund, with 50% of the net annual income being added to the fund. The remaining 50% is to be used to offset capital and or operating expenditures.
