By 1993, following legal advice, the fund was renamed as the Contingency and Development Fund and administered by the Board of Directors. To avoid tax implications, 100% of the net income is added to the operating income of the company.

entries.title: History
entries.description: Dr John Price volunteered to help write a History of Maracaibo and requested interesting stories and photos. In 1970 it was decided to build a tennis court as long as the cost did not exceed $1,000! It obviously did and we ended up Pickleball Courts. Dianne Price tells us her family was the first to stay in an A frame after Maracaibo was formed.

entries.title: Basketball hoops
entries.description: Basketball hoops installed at the Pickleball courts

entries.title: Gazebo
entries.description: The Gazebo designed and built by Eddy and Simon Jang and Charles Bazzard proved a great success and a shady haven on a sunny day. It has been used as a venue for a wedding, several wedding receptions, Olympics dances, Christmas carol singing and a potluck centre. (In the photo Simon is on the roof unveiling the eagle at the 1991 Olympic opening ceremony. King Howard is on the left. The lumber was milled from trees from District lot 8.

entries.title: Olympics 91
entries.description: This was the 15th annual Olympics. The following is an extract from a letter from Patty Vogel, who donated a recycled silver cup to be presented to the winning team captains each year. “This trophy is given on behalf of all those who were at the founding games in 1976. In later games it was my responsibility to obtain prizes, usually from the Thrift shop. I do wish to mark the 15th year of the holding of the games and to discharge my obligation of giving prizes of recycled junk at future games! The trophy is to be held at Maracaibo and be given in memory of the fun the founding members families have had and have at Maracaibo and the games.”

entries.title: Workboat replaced
entries.description: The Old 20 was sold to Henry Boudin and a new workboat was purchased

entries.title: Maracaibo Golf Tournament
entries.description: Golf Tournament started by Gundy and Ann McLeod. 29 Members played in a “Texas Scramble”. 44 members attended an excellent buffet at the Golf Club after the tournament. The winners were Cathy Campbell, Gundy McLeod and Gary Tremblay, who received a lovely perpetual trophy donated by Anne McLeod. (photo is of subsequent winners – the Rowell’s and Le Moines)

entries.title: Grey Whale
entries.description: A grey whale came down Long Harbour and breached 20 ft from the outer float of the docks as Becky Bazzard and Tiffany Tremblay were walking down. (picture shows a Grey or Humpback whale off the docks in 2007 – bottom right)

entries.title: Weddings
entries.description: 3 weddings were held at Maracaibo making for a busy September

entries.title: Cablevision
entries.description: An extraordinary general meeting of the strata lot was held to approve the installation of Cablevision. Installed by Salt Spring Cablevision at a cost of $60,000 to Maracaibo strata lot owners. The motion to approve was narrowly defeated. Subsequently approval was gained at the AGM. A loan agreement was granted from Maracaibo Estates Ltd to allow Members not connecting to delay payment until either connection or sale of property. Salt Spring Cablevision was subsequently sold to Shaw. In retrospect 25 years later the decision to go with cable rather than satellites was a good one.

entries.title: Trail Guide
entries.description: The first trail guide was developed

entries.title: ME President- Harvey Wright
entries.description: Harvey was elected as president and served in that role until 1994. During Harveys time attention was payed to upgrading and improving Maracaibo’s facilities. By the end of 1993 there were 44 houses built in the Strata and 50 members with homes on Salt Spring. With 109 families owning the 128 issued shares the demand for cottage rentals begins to decline. Demand for dock space increases however.

entries.title: AGM 1992
entries.description: AGM was held at the Shaughnessy Golf Club Howard Martin stepped down from the Board of Directors having served since the inaugural meeting in April 1970. Howard was on the Advisory committee from 1970 to 1976. He was the first President of Maracaibo and stayed in that role to 1982 overseeing the development of Phase I of District Lot 8 and Phase 1 of the Strata Plan. No wonder he was named King Howard with 21 years of service to Maracaibo! Annual dues increased to $650. The large increase was due to the fact that investment income was not being included in operating income (this soon changes).

entries.title: Mission Statement
entries.description: in 1992 a two day board retreat was held for the first time. It was then that the Board adopted a Mission Statement of What Maracaibo is (developed in 1987 from a focus group of Members) It was also decided to put a 3 year moratorium on considering any further land development. Inheritance problems were also a major part of the discussions.

entries.title: Gerry Ringrose
entries.description: Gerry Ringrose was hired as a part time gardener. We soon found out that he had a vast number of talents, including being highly entertaining, and he worked for us for a few years. He built the enclosure over Indian Well, The arbour to the dock and the arbour at the main house amongst many other projects. Jerry is a very accomplished stain glass craftsman.

entries.title: Cottage names
entries.description: The cottages known as #1, #2,#3 and #4 were renamed Arbutus, Balsam Cedar and Dogwood.

entries.title: Dock Extension
entries.description: 100 ft additional moorage floats added – and 200 ft replaced. Maracaibo moorage had been increased from 30 lineal ft in 1970 to 1400 ft, 1200 lineal ft being built by staff. New pilings were added and water and power extended

entries.title: Round Prevost sailboat race
entries.description: An impromptu Round Prevost sailboat race had been held informally for a number of years but in 1992 it became an official annual event followed by a potluck supper at the Barn. For some it was taken very seriously and for others it was a good opportunity to use a catapult to fire at competing boats. An interesting handicap system was developed over the years based on a variety of factors including previous performance. For example Jenny Wren had a 3 day handicap but never won.

entries.title: Water Utility
entries.description: The Maracaibo Water Utility was taken over by the Strata Corporation. This means that accounting is simpler (one less legal entity). Running Maracaibo’s community water system requires management on a daily basis, continual education maintenance and upgrading

entries.title: Water System Extension
entries.description: A water main extension was installed in the Core Area with a connection from the works yard to a fire hydrant close to the barn.

entries.title: Telephones installed in Cottages
entries.description: in 2020 it is hard to imagine that telephones had not been installed in the cottages sooner. The members came to Maracaibo to get away from the fast pace of city life and not having a phone was part of the charm. However it meant that the managers were constantly having to deliver messages. For a few years we used an intercom system from the office to the cottages, but that was not without problems.

entries.title: Workshop
entries.description: The Worksyard area was expanded to create room for a decent sized workshop. This was designed and built by staff using timber milled from the property.

entries.title: Property Assessments Appeal
entries.description: Property Assessments appealed en masse due to 40% plus increases on waterfront properties. B.C. Assessment authority lowered assessments after appeal and presentation from the manager. They also conceded that the value of a Maracaibo share should not be included in the property assessment.

entries.title: AGM 1993
entries.description: The AGM was held at the Shaughnessy Golf Club. Highlights were: Cablevision connections have commenced A change in philosophy for the use of investment income was adopted by the Directors to avoid high tax on investment income E.J. Oliver and Associates are appointed as investment managers for the Contingency and Development funds previously designated as the Heritage Fund. Resolution approved by strata lot owners for Maracaibo Estates Ltd to obtain a right of first refusal to purchase Fisherman’s Island and grant Dick Newman various rights in return including access over the Common Land. Report made on Neighbourhood Watch – trespassing on common land discussed

entries.title: A Frame Cottages bathroom additions
entries.description: By adding an extension to the roof of Balsam and Cedar Cottages we were able to create standing room for a shower in the baths. The rest of the bathroom was renovated at the same time.

entries.title: Easter
entries.description: Participants in the hunt!

entries.title: Tidal Grid
entries.description: A tidal grid was built to allow members to clean and paint the bottom of their boats. Tide level fluctuations due to high and low pressure systems resulted in the level of the grid being higher than optimal.

entries.title: Pickleball Court
entries.description: The surface was repaired and repainted

entries.title: Tidal Grid in Use
entries.description: The tidal grid works well with the right conditions, It is best suited to full keel boats.

entries.title: Road Safety and Trespassing
entries.description: It was agreed that speed signs be increased, a centre line be painted in strategic places along the road and identification stickers be given to members for their cars

entries.title: Cablevision in Cottages
entries.description: After surveying members it was decided not to install cablevision in the cottages. Members who wanted TV continued to bring there own and hope the rabbit ear antennae worked.

entries.title: Road Safety and Trespassing
entries.description: It was agreed that speed signs be increased, a centre line be painted in strategic places along the road and identification stickers be given to members for their cars

entries.title: Cablevision in Cottages
entries.description: After surveying members it was decided not to install cablevision in the cottages. Members who wanted TV continued to bring there own and hope the rabbit ear antennae worked.

entries.title: Dock Arbour
entries.description: The entrance to the dock was improved with new flagstones installed, rock walls on the flowerbeds and a rose arbour built.

entries.title: Traffic Survey
entries.description: A two hour traffic survey by volunteers at the entrance of Maracaibo recorded a vehicle every 3 minutes. Many Members were not displaying the Maracaibo M sticker but there was only one unauthorised visit from a” look-ee-loo”.

entries.title: Olympics 93
entries.description: An innovative way to light the Olympic flame! Pip Bazzard in the bucket. The Backhoe was driven by Christian Blagborne a lot faster than Charles would have liked! The large numbers of teenagers has declined but a successful Nose Point Relay was held after much persuasion to get enough runners. There were about 270 attendees for the BBQ

entries.title: Sea wall
entries.description: The wall was extended west of the dock walkway to offset rapid erosion of the foreshore.

entries.title: Barn accommodation proposal
entries.description: A suggestion to convert the barn into a multipurpose centre was reviewed. The conversion would have involved a total rebuild with suggestions to include a storage area, a meeting area and small rental accommodation above. A survey was circulated showing two options one with accommodation and one without. Much discussion ensued with strong support for option II of the Barn conversion, but the proposal was tabled, subject to further review as it was felt that a thorough review of all development options for siting of facilities in the Core Area needed to be carried out. Gerard Farry and Charles Bazzard were asked to co-chair a committee to determine siting option recommendations for future development. In 1994 Bob Hassell and Leslie DeAthe Joined Gerard and Charles. The findings of this committee are set out in the Directions for Maracaibo’s future which was circulated in 1995.

entries.title: Islands Trust – Community Plan
entries.description: The Islands Trust is reviewing the community plan and discussing lowering development density for future developments. This would affect Maracaibo’s undeveloped land and the manager attended multiple meetings to ensure Maracaibo’s interests were maintained.

entries.title: Post Boxes
entries.description: Post office boxes are located at the corner of Mansell and Robinson Road. The post office decides to install more boxes and wants the Strata Corporation to pay for the boxes to be placed at the entrance to Maracaibo. Maracaibo objects and after some negotiation the Post Office relents and agrees to pay for the boxes to be located inside Maracaibo if Maracaibo clears the location. Done!

entries.title: 25th Anniversary Planning
entries.description: Claire Pickering chairs committee of Members planning a variety of ways to celebrate Maracaibo’s 25th to be held in 1995.

entries.title: Hydro Line – Broom – Christmas Tree farm
entries.description: BC Hydro slashed all the vegetation on the powerline, using an excavator and rotary mower. They left about 5 acres untouched that Maracaibo was using as a Christmas tree farm. What we did not realize until a few years later was that the soil disturbance created by the excavator and the removal of natural vegetation created the perfect environment for broom to flourish and spread. An ecological disaster along powerlines all over Vancouver Island!

entries.title: Weather Report
entries.description: Brian Cornwall was the official weather record keeper for a number of years. This was the 1993 report June to December.

entries.title: ME President – John Pickering
entries.description: Picture of John Pickering cooking pancake. John Initiated the move of Directors meetings to Salt Spring in 1995, and the AGM 1996. 1994 – 1996 was an extremely busy time for the Maracaibo Board with lots of planning initiatives, organization of Board duties, the Anniversary celebrations and new infrastructure construction projects were carried out.

entries.title: AGM ’94
entries.description: It was noted that the highlight of the AGM was Quentin Brown’s decription of Billy Butlins holiday camps in the UK and his hope that the master plan for the core area would not envisage any similarities.

entries.title: Directors Meetings
entries.description: All of The Directors meetings were held at Maracaibo. Previously they were held in various locations in Vancouver.

entries.title: Strata Special General Meeting
entries.description: To approve application for a Water Lease for the Dock located opposite the Fisherman’s Island

entries.title: Eagles and Geese
entries.description: Geese have become a major problem in the meadows. We purchased two large plastic eagles to scare them off. In Newsletter #55 we noted that “We saw a young eagle sitting next to one of the models, and the seagulls and crows are most indignant, so we are quite optimistic.” The geese did stay away for a while but they soon adapted and ignored the eagles.

entries.title: Selective logging
entries.description: Cedar and fir were selectively logged in District Lot 8 to provide a source of lumber for a number of construction projects planned at Maracaibo. The logging was completed by the end of September, but the milling continued through the summer of 1995.

entries.title: Boat Ramp
entries.description: The Boat Ramp was extended and a retaining wall built on one side. A rock breakwater to the east allowed boats to be launched in calm water.

entries.title: 25th Anniversary Committee
entries.description: Committee Members – Claire Pickering, Laurel Gordon, Elizabeth Beckmann, Anne Little, Gary Brady, Maureen Rowell, Liz Farry, Gary Tremblay, Charles and Sally Bazzard, are planning a variety of ways to celebrate in 1995. The main event will be a dinner dance for 300. Other ideas being considered are: a treasure hunt; a car rally; open houses; a history book; a recipe book; Maracaibo clothing. Response to a reuest for photos and stories were sparse.

entries.title: 94 Olympics
entries.description: One of the highlight was a new event in the pool – “The Greasy Pole”

entries.title: Cottages -Cablevision
entries.description: Arbutus Balsam and Cedar Cottages receive cablevision connections but no TV’s are provided. It was not long before Maracibo purchased some small portable TV’s that were rented out for $5 a day. It was a chore for the staff continually moving TV’s around. Several years later TV’s were located permanently in each cottage except Clamshell.

entries.title: Maracaibo Logo
entries.description: Moira McLeod designed a new Logo for Maracaibo free of charge and it is going to be used on clothing to be sold as a fundraiser for the 25th Anniversary celebrations. The Logo became the official Maracaibo emblem for several years.

entries.title: New Well
entries.description: A new well is added to the water system to boost supply as the number of homes steadily increases.

entries.title: Board of Directors
entries.description: One of the few photos of the Board. We wish we had taken one every year.

entries.title: Logo Clothing
entries.description: Orders for clothing are being taken in time for Christmas

entries.title: AGM 1995
entries.description: There was much debate about moving future meetings to Salt Spring as the number of Members able to attend on Salt Spring is equal to those in Vancouver. Annual Dues are $550 and Strata Fees $470. A resolution was passed to allow spouses of strata lot owners to be elected to the strata council.

entries.title: Core Area Planning – Task Force
entries.description: An update and scope of the project was reviewed by the Board of Directors and circulated to the Members. The Planning Task Force were asked to extend their planning mandate to include all facets of Maracaibo.

entries.title: Easter 1995
entries.description: Members gather after the Easter Egg Hunt for coffee and hot cross buns and to buy 25th anniversary clothing

entries.title: Logo Clothing Sales
entries.description: The McLeods headed a group of members promoting the sale of Maracaibo logo clothing. The sale of these went so well that $3000 was generated for the celebrations.

entries.title: Members and Lot Owners
entries.description: The following is a pdf link to the Members and lot owners in April 1995 Members and Lot Owners April 1995

entries.title: Directions for Maracaibo’s Future
entries.description: The Planning Task Force’s report was circulated to the Members. This was the culmination of many meetings including input from focus groups on Salt Spring and in Vancouver. At the June Directors meetings they agreed in principal with all of the suggestions as set out by the planning group and agreed to implement the following as soon as possible. 1. Establishing a Land Resources Committee to produce a Land Management Plan. 2. Assigning pollution prevention reponsibilities to the Water Management Committee. 3. Establish a committee to research security matters 4. Whole Board to discuss aging assets 5. Convert the downstairs bedroom of the Main House into a Members lounge 6. A committe formed to prepare development guidelines for the Core Area. 7. Vehicle and Equipment Storage to be constucted in the worksyard adjoining the workshop. 8. Board to review membership share options. 9. The Goals, Objectives and Vision of Maracaibo be reviewed. 10. Erosion control at the base of the cliffs be extended. (Pdf copy of report link below.) Directions for Maracaibo’s Future

entries.title: Eddy’s Playground
entries.description: Eddy Jang enjoyed building the children’s playground so much we named it “Eddy’s Playground”.

entries.title: Anniversary Invitation
entries.description: There was a great response to Invitations to the anniversary dinner dance. The aim of the Anniversary committee was to build on the existing community spirit at Maracaibo, involve as many Members as possible and foster a variety of events that would allow the Members to get to know each other and Maracaibo better.

entries.title: Spring into Summer Breakfast
entries.description: Gundy McLeod organised the first pancake breakfast that soon became a Maracaibo tradition held on the closest Saturday to Canada Day. (In the photo is Murray Sumpton making pancakes). This idea was also part of the Anniversary celebrations.

entries.title: Coffee Mornings
entries.description: Laurel Gordon pioneered the idea of Members holding coffee mornings in their homes. In 1995 the following members hosted coffee mornings: The Farrys, Littles, J Price, Gordon/Sumpton, Reimers, Mundys, Nye/ Cornwall, Wellmans and McLeods. Coffee mornings continue to be a very popular event and enables members to meet each other and enjoy visiting other homes at Maracaibo. There are usually two a year.

entries.title: Anniversary set up
entries.description: Claire Pickering setting tables. The Anniversay dinner / dance was attended by 297 Members and family representing 70% of the Membership. The event was held in a very large marquee. A many of the founding members attended. Special guests included Goody Goodman who had worked as a gardner / caretaker at Maracaibo in the 1930’s. Migs Edwards and Mary Moat, previous owners of the properties. Quentin Brown was there but John Lansdell was unable to attend. Tom and Yvonne Toynbee were also present.

entries.title: Anniversary Reception
entries.description: Peter Rowell (Md) MC did a wonderful job as MC for the reception, despite his humerous annoucement that he thought everyone was their to celebrate his retirement from general practice. The dinner and speeches (which had to be cut short) were followed by a Directors Skit. This was followed by dancing to music from a DJ and then fireworks at midnight. Charles had forgotten about fireworks going bang and they caused quite a stir in the Long Harbour community. There were a few irate phone messages.

entries.title: Anniversary Founding Members
entries.description: So happy to have the original owners of the property at the party – Migs Edwards and Mary Moat

entries.title: Garry Oak seedlings
entries.description: Member Don Reimer donated a Gary Oak seedling with planting instructions for every family attending the dinner. As long as the seedlings were protected from browsing deer several survived.

entries.title: Treasure Hunt
entries.description: Winners of the Treasure Hunt were the Cooper family. The prize was a beautiful chest built by Gary Tremblay, full of all sorts of loot!

entries.title: Anniversary Skit
entries.description: This is what the Directors looked like for their 2020 skit. Clockwise – Liz Farry, Gordon Trueman, Maureen Rowell, Dick Vogel, Ian Jessiman, John Price and Lauel Gordon. The skit depicting an all female board, was hilarious. The topic being discussed was contamination in the swimming lagoon from the new Core Area development.

entries.title: Anniversary Skit
entries.description: A look into the future. This is what the Directors thought Charles would look like in 2020. If the 2020 Covid 19 isolation continues the haircut will be right!

entries.title: The Pavillion
entries.description: There was an information meeting held at Maracaibo to discuss a proposal for a multi purpose pavillion to be located close to the pickle ball courts. Comments were received for and against the project. It was decided that a review would be carried out and no further work done.

entries.title: Computer Age!
entries.description: Microsoft introduces Windows 95 and computer use becomes much more accessible. Newsletter #64 is the first Newsletter created on a computer!

entries.title: Members Meeting Lounge
entries.description: It was decided to explore conversion of the downstairs bedroom in the Main House and fronting patio as space for Members to meet and play Bridge. It was also decided that a cottage could be used mid week for Members to use for this.

entries.title: Boat Covered Storage
entries.description: A Covered boat storage facility with 7 bays was constructed in the boatyard All of the bays were immediately rented by Members with a waiting list on hand. This project was also built by staff using lumber milled from the property.

entries.title: Mail Boxes
entries.description: A roof over the mailboxes and notice boards were built by staff.

entries.title: Capital Expenditures
entries.description: 1995 was a very busy year and it’s interesting to note in the financial statements that the following capital expense projects were completed: equipment storage buildings in the worksyard, covered boat storage shed, additional dock and walkway at Indian Well Beach, lengthening the breakwater float at the marina, construction of the childrens’ playground, purchase of a new computer and photocopier for the office, purchase of major tools for the workshop, milling lumber, consultancy for erosion planning. All of this was achieved for a capital cost of $45,733.24!

entries.title: Members Lounge proposal
entries.description: A proposal to convert the downstairs bedroom and bathroom of the Main House is explained in the following pdf Members Lounge 96

entries.title: AGM
entries.description: The AGM was held on Salt Spring for the first time. There was a record turnout with over 80 members attending. 27 Members attended a pre-meeting in Vancouver – Approval was given to change the year end of from September 30th to December 31st – Proposal to renovate the Main House to create a Members lounge and patio was approved and to be financed by a special assessment of $40 a year for 5 years.

entries.title: ME President – Dr John Price
entries.description: This was the second time that John played a major roll in management having previously chaired the Advisory Committee in the late 1970’s. Unfortunately John’s term was cut short due to ill health.

entries.title: Fire Box
entries.description: The first fire box, containing fire fighting equipment, is located by Clamshell Cottage.

entries.title: Members Lounge
entries.description: Official opening of the new Members Lounge – picture shows Maureen Rowell, Liz Farry and John Price cutting the ribbon. The room, and especially the patio, proved a great success. It was used for Bridge, Happy Hours and Directors meetings. On special occasions it opened into the Managers lounge which was used for bigger functions. For the Managers a new entrance to the office was a major benefit as Members could now enter directly to the office without going through the front hall of the house. The lower foundation log was replaced with a concrete footing. Paving stones were installed on the patio and the arbour built from cedar milled at Maracaibo. Gerry Ringrose was the inspiration behind the arbour and paving stones and rock wall for the flowerbed. Eddy Jang used his amazing inginuity to replace the foundation logs and install a proper foundation as well as the interior changes including cutting out a section of log wall to install french doors. A small kitchen was installed in the old walk-in closet, cabinets built by Eddy, and the bathroom converted into an entrance lobby with powder room adjoining.

entries.title: Office Reno
entries.description: The Office entrance changed as a result of the creation of the Members Lounge. Members could now enter the office directly instead of through the front hall. Eddy Jang built a counter with storage cupboards and a new desk for Sally.

entries.title: Olympics 1996
entries.description: This is the 20th Maracaibo Olympics. The demographics are changing at Maracaibo and the need to focus on exhausting our teenagers on the August long weekend is replaced by the need to entertain a growing number of young children. The Nose Point Relay, Marathon and Triathlon are replaced with events more suited to a younger generation of participants. A committee is formed to help the managers organise the events. Bob Quart arranged for Van City’s Fat Cat mascot to entertain at the opening ceremony.

entries.title: Kayaks
entries.description: The Maracaibo Boat Club purchases a kayak and David Mundy donates his kayak to the club. Kayaks prove more popular than canoes. Windsurfers are virtually a thing of the past. What will the next trend be? Photo shows the Olympic flame arriving via Kayak.

entries.title: The Bouy at Mariners Lane
entries.description: Dick Vogel found a buoy and felt it would go well at the Mariners Lane entrance to accompany the anchor. Dick calls Charles and says “all you have to do is go to Capital Iron in Victoria and they will load it in your truck, it is all arranged and paid for!” Charles set off to pick it up with the 1 ton truck. The bottom of the buoy is filled with concrete, so when it was first placed in the truck with the heaviest end at the back, the front wheels lifted off the ground. When it was turned around the front wheels stayed on the ground but the steering was very light going up hill! Charles made it back to Salt Spring after a harrowing journey and the bouy was duly installed. Dick was right – the combination anchor, bouy and chain at the entrance to Mariners Lane is a great addition.

entries.title: Maracaibo Golf
entries.description: Golf continues to be very popular. Photo at Golf Club dinner. The McLeods continue to do a great job organising and gathering prizes. A highlight in 96 was when Earle Morriss won one of the baseball hats he had donated. When he put it on it split in two with the brim resting on his nose, causing much laughter from the group.

entries.title: Round Prevost Race
entries.description: This was probably the pinnacle year with 14 boats participating. the following is an extract from newsletter #69. ” There was considerable pressure on ‘Caviar’ (Charles, Pip and Earle) to win and rumours that she would be rammed at the start, so she kept well clear of the other boats and made the mistake of heading south. Glomerus and Tillicum 1 chose the better course heading along the shore of Prevost and streaked ahead of the fleet, most of whom had followed Caviar expecting Charles to have superior tactics (big mistake!) Eventually Caviar clawed her way back to the leaders and moved ahead in light winds half way around Prevost and went on to win.”

entries.title: Main House upgrades
entries.description: Much of the 1950s carpeting was replaced in the Main House, and the sliding glass door to the conservatory was replaced with a French door.

entries.title: Telephone code change
entries.description: The Code for Salt Spring changes from 604 to 250

entries.title: Dock at Indian Well
entries.description: Due to a big storm in November one of the float anchors parted and two pilings were promptly installed to secure the dock and walkway.

entries.title: The Blizzard of ’96
entries.description: The snow started on Boxing Day afternoon. The Bazzards were away skiing and caught the last ferry back that night. Eddy and Simon Jang had been ploughing the roads. Charles took over and ploughed until 1.00 am.

entries.title: The Blizzard aftermath
entries.description: It took three days to dig out from the heaviest snow storm on record. The snow was so thick that only the roads ploughed late the previous night could be ploughed. An army of members turned out to help us open up the roads. Day 1 – we cleared Nose Point Road and Mariners Lane. Day 2 – We broke through Mansell Road and Seclusion Lane. John Pickering went ahead on his tractor creating a trail to follow and allow traction for the snowplough truck which was grounding out! Day 3 – We tackled Kingfisher and Fisherman’s Lanes and a few driveways.

entries.title: Blizzard Evacuation
entries.description: Becky Bazzard and Jerry Shrive used the work boat to evacuate Kingfisher lane residents from the beach over to Scott Point so they could catch the ferry back to Vancouver. Some Members were headed to a New Years Eve concert with Pavarotti at BC Place. Most of the damage occurred New Years Eve due to flooding caused by a quick thaw. The works yard access was washed out and Kingfisher Lane Culverts could not handle the load and the pressure of water caused erosion on the lots. Subsequently an extra culvert was installed and drainage ditches and pipes installed across affected lots.

entries.title: Emergency Response Plan
entries.description: Following the Blizzard of ’96 we developed an emergency response plan accessible to Members and Staff.

entries.title: Business / Financial Plan
entries.description: The Planning Task group is asked to present the members with the issues that Maracaibo is facing in the future and options for them to consider. 11 gatherings are arranged with 10 – 15 shareholders at each of these. By November Members representing 102 of the 128 issued shares had attended the presentations. Photo Planning Group Charles Bazzard, Gerard Farry, Bob Hassell and Leslie DeAthe head to Vancouver for a presentation – accompanied by Gundy McLeod and Ian Jessiman. (insert pdf Business Plan draft) BusinessPlan Draft

entries.title: Maracaibo History
entries.description: Charles and Sally are in the editing stage. Donna Reimer volunteered to help with editing and Publication.

entries.title: Salt Spring Island Community
entries.description: After much public input and major input from Maracaibo. The Islands Trust moderated the proposed Community Plan changes to one that gained broad acceptance.

entries.title: Erosion Control
entries.description: After several years of negotiating with the Ministry of Environment we obtained permission to complete erosion control work at the base of the cliffs in front of the cottages.

entries.title: Emergency Phone Chain and Fire Practices
entries.description: The phone-out system with coordinators for each sector of the development is working well. Two fire practices were held during the summer and Maracaibo is gradually building up a supply of fire fighting equipment.

entries.title: President – Les Little
entries.description: ME President – Les Little took over as President from Dr John Price who stepped back due to health issues. Les brought great experience to the Board, and his taxation expertise was particularly beneficial. Les, a keen gardener, organised the purchase of some new deciduous trees to be planted in the Core Area. Another project that Les started was the Maracaibo Directory with pictures of Members and contact information.

entries.title: Trincomali Trail
entries.description: John Graham blazed a route for this trail and Summer staff worked on making it accessible. More challenging than most of the trails, this one allows access to an area that would otherwise be unexplored.

entries.title: Olympics 1997
entries.description: Another successful event

entries.title: Members Workshop
entries.description: A workshop facilitated by Leslie Deathe allowed discussion on the three components of a Business Plan. 35 Members took part providing valuable feedback.

entries.title: Members Survey
entries.description: A survey was sent to all Members. The survey established the goals and objectives of the Members and their attitudes towards a number of issues. Leslie DeAthe was key in designing and analyzing the survey and its results. The Survey Highlights were circulated in February 1998 (PDF) Survey Highlights

entries.title: Ground Water Geologist report
entries.description: A Groundwater Geologist – Anne Badry completed a review of the overall water capacity of the wells at Maracaibo

entries.title: Business Plan Committee
entries.description: A committee made up of Les Little, Don Graham, Adlai Rust, Leslie DeAthe, Gary Tremblay and Charles Bazzard are preparing a 5 year Business Plan

entries.title: AGM
entries.description: The meeting was held at the Lions Club on Salt Spring Island, followed by dinner at the Seacourt Restaurant in present day Gasoline Alley (Humperdinck’s) The dinner with dancing after was a great success. Highlight of the meeting was a presentation of the survey results.

entries.title: Land Management
entries.description: Don Reimer, Board member and professional forester, volunteered his services and staff time to prepare a base information plan of the Maracaibo property. Don has plotted 3D information showing contours , slopes, vegetation, property lines, roads and water system information. Don and his crew, helped by members, staked out 80 identification plots randomly across the peninsula. The purpose was to inventory and measure major species, particularly trees, within a 20ft radius. This work laid the basis for the Land Management Plan. Photo Don Reimer third from left, staff and members before setting out to stake out plots.

entries.title: War on Broom
entries.description: An Honour Roll of Members who had joined the war on broom was displayed. Keith and Chris Galloway, Sally and Glen Rycroft and Peter and Joyce Sharpe were instigators of many volunteer broom removal sessions. Many lot owners joined the weekly gatherings in May and part of June. These broom parties continued through the mid 2000s. Photo taken 2010 of a celebration on the powerline after a successful broom pulling season.

entries.title: Tennis Courts and Pickleball courts resurfaced
entries.description: Tennis is still very popular with the highlight being the annual tournament held in May each year. Picture shows Lounge in the Main House set up for dinner. Pickleball continues to be very popular too, mainly with the teenagers

entries.title: Painting the Main House
entries.description: Eddy Jang and Pip Bazzard painting the Main House

entries.title: Swimming Lagoon Cleanup
entries.description: Some years when the tides and weather cooperate it is possible to do a major cleanup by removing the soft mud from the bottom of the lagoon.

entries.title: Film Site
entries.description: Maracaibo registered with the B.C. Film Board as a possible film site. We never heard back. PDF Film Site Promo Film Site

entries.title: Non Potable Water
entries.description: Water from the works yard well is still smelly. The groundwater geologist recommends we continue to pump water from the well to help remediate the problem. An old concrete water storage tank above the Core Area was patched and a roof installed. Waterlines were then connected from the well to the tank and water gravity fed to irrigate the gardens in the Core Area and to be used for boat and car washing. This worked very well, the smell from the water dissipated as it aerated going into the water tank, and after 10 more years of use the smell problem decreased sufficiently to allow the water to be used as potable water in the main supply system. Photo – installing roof on old reservoir.

entries.title: New Float
entries.description: We replaced the float at Indian Well beach with a new one

entries.title: Docks
entries.description: Approximately 1/3 of the Members have a boat that is either kept at Maracaibo or used for summertime visits. Capital expenses for docks, up until 1998, totalled $130,000. Moorage revenue in 1997 was $27,308.

entries.title: Olympics 1998
entries.description: Another successful Olympics with approximately 250 attending the BBQ. It was noted that we had not seen the Core Area so busy since the early 1980s due to an influx of grandchildren!

entries.title: Fall weather
entries.description: Beautiful weather all fall meant that the meadows were still being mowed at the end of October

entries.title: Magic of Maracaibo
entries.description: The book is finally off to the publishers and will be ready for sale in time for Christmas. The work involved in writing a historical book, researching and making judgements about what might be of interest was a lot more challenging than Charles and Sally anticipated. Donna Reimer was a great help with editing and book design. Barnyard Grafix arranged the cover design and printing. The Littles gave permission to use a Carole Evans painting on the front cover. Ed Davis took the aerial photo on the back cover.

entries.title: Carol Singing and Hay Ride
entries.description: Carol-singing took place under the Gazebo proceeded by a hay ride from the Main House to the entrance and back. The Hay ride proved popular and continued for several years until one time coming down the hill to the core area the tractor gear popped out and the tractor, towing a 20ft trailer with 50 people on board, had to descend on brakes alone. The passengers were unaware, but the driver was terrified! That was the last hay ride down a steep hill.

entries.title: Clamshell Deck Replacement
entries.description: Simon Jang returned to help replace the deck at Clamshell Cottage.

entries.title: Weather
entries.description: It was a very windy and wet winter. On February 5th there was a dramatic rescue of a boat by the Coastguard. A sailboat broke its mooring line and drifted into some pilings. The owner managed to board her and got clear of the pilings. Unfortunately a line went overboard and tangled in the propeller and she was pounded on the rocks in front of Cedar Cottage. It was the height of the windstorm with gusts recorded at 155 kmh. The owner got to shore and the Coastguard pulled the boat off with minimal damage.

entries.title: Master Woodland Managers program
entries.description: Charles signs up for the first group to be trained as Woodland Managers in B.C. The project is sponsored through UBC using facilities at their research property in Black Creek, Cowichan Lake and Malaspina College. The program is modeled after a similar program in Oregon. The education is invaluable to Charles in planning land management for Maracaibo.

entries.title: Barn Conversion
entries.description: Eddy and Simon Jang worked together to convert the barn, originally built for cows and equipment in the 1930s. A concrete floor was poured, new porch added, plus beams, posts and new roof.

entries.title: AGM
entries.description: The AGM was moved back to the Harbour House Hotel where the new Wheel House room was the best venue to accommodate our meeting and dinner needs. Two reports were given . 1. Don Reimer – a synopsis on the Land Stewardship Plan. 2. Charles Bazzard – Security solutions. Constable West of the RCMP gave an overview of the crime situation on the Island. In the last few months a Maracaibo home had been robbed of several First Nations artwork and three outboard motors had been stolen from the works yard. Photos were taken of Members attending the AGM to be used in the Members Directory.

entries.title: Goody’s Barn
entries.description: The barn has been the centre for many events since its conversion. Pancake breakfasts, Olympics BBQ’s, wedding ceremonies, receptions and various parties. A place to play table tennis and an area to watch TV. The old workshop on the side was converted into a room for catering. Goody’s Barn was named after Goody Goodman who was the caretaker at Maracaibo in the early 1930’s. Goody used to keep a cow in the barn and he lived in the original house built by Ross Mahon near the boat ramp. Eddy Jang lived with Goody when he first came to Salt Spring and is still treated as one of Goody’s family.

entries.title: Boat Yard – Motors Stolen
entries.description: Several outboard motors were stolen off boats in the yard. The culprits entered the area from Rain Forest Road and used a skiff to haul the motors over the bank to the road. The thieves had come from Duncan and were caught by the RCMP. This happened while we were at the Annual General Meeting in Ganges!

entries.title: Broom Clearing
entries.description: Congratulations to Graham Clay for clearing broom from Mariners Lane to the Nose Point turnaround, Don Longley and family for various pulling expeditions, Julie Elizabeth and the Quarts for battling Kingfisher Lane broom and Michael Van Straubenzee, Simon Lord and John and Noreen Davies.

entries.title: Nature Walk
entries.description: A new nature trail was developed leading off the Rainforest trail. Harold Macy from UBC forestry research led a members’ walk with Charles to identify and discuss the forest. Charles had recently qualified as a Master Woodland Manager on a course designed by Harold.

entries.title: Canada Day Pancake Breakfast
entries.description: The first breakfast held in the newly renovated barn, Organized by Gundy McLeod and his cooking crew of Murray Sumpton, Greg Slakov and Don Longley . At least 42 members attended. The highlight was Karen and Nick Slakov (6 and 51/2) leading us in singing O Canada.

entries.title: Security Survey
entries.description: The responses and comments were circulated to members see pdf. Security Survey 1999

entries.title: Road Safety
entries.description: Road safety and speeding continue to be a concern. An engineer was hired to review our road and lines of visibility and confirmed that the road was safe as built for a design speed of 30 KMH. Log barriers were place along Nose Point road and Rainforest Road at steep drop-off points. These are more a visual deterrent, but appeared to have satisfactory result.

entries.title: New Years Eve – New Millenium
entries.description: Many members celebrated at their homes in Maracaibo and the cottages were full. This group celebrated in Arbutus Cottage and have spent numerous New Years together.

entries.title: AGM – Land Stewardship report
entries.description: Don Reimer and Charles are working on a Woodland Management Plan. Plans for thinning the forest in District Lot 8 are put on hold due to the Texada Logging controversy on the south end of Salt Spring.

entries.title: AGM – Road safety
entries.description: Road signs and safety was a hot topic. A new sign at the entrance to Maracaibo had been chopped down! Reasons were given and it was recognised that reactive policymaking was not achieving the desired effect. As a consequence several signs were removed and centre lines painted on the road in danger areas. Everyone is aware of the problem of speeding but it continues.

entries.title: Members Directory
entries.description: The first Directories with photos of Members were distributed at the AGM

entries.title: Dr Graham Clay – President
entries.description: Graham was elected as President Chairman. Graham loved Maracaibo. When he was not being a surgeon in Vancouver he spent as much time as possible at his home at Maracaibo. A keen gardener Graham also enjoyed his building process. Graham served as Chairman until 2006

entries.title: Cottages
entries.description: The Roof of Cedar cottage was replaced – James Sinclair worked on that, before being employed by Maracaibo. Post and beam porches with glass roofs were added to Balsam and Cedar cottages.

entries.title: Docks
entries.description: A new breakwater float is constructed with a lower float for the lasers and canoes to be pulled onto. The new floats as seen at the 2000 Olympics.

entries.title: Geese
entries.description: The geese, 40 of them, have been a real menace. Fencing was erected across the meadows to discourage them from landing and all along the access points on the shoreline. Eventually they moved to Mansell Farm.

entries.title: Aussie Olympics
entries.description: The Olympics are evolving to cater to a younger group of Members children and grandchildren. As the actual Olympics are being held in Sidney Australia we adopted an Australian theme complete with a kangaroo, and joey(courtesy of the Williams). Over 300 attended the BBQ Afterwards, Tim Beckmann led a group of young men, all bribed with the promise of free beer, in singing “Tie me Kangaroo down Sport” and ” Waltzing Matilda.”

entries.title: Fun and Games at the Barn
entries.description: Joan Winstanley celebrated a big birthday in style! Everyone dressed in the 50s theme. Marilyn Monroe sang her famous “Happy Birthday”. David Niven was there and so was Zora and Lucille Ball plus several greasers and their girls and some English schoolboys. Charles shaved off his beard and with long sideburns and his old school boater caused quite a stir. The boys lined up to dance with Marilyn!

entries.title: Golf Tournament
entries.description: The Millennium Golf Day was a success with 36 golfer, and 56 attending the buffet diner. The major excitement was having a go for a $20,000 prize for anyone getting a hole in one on the 6th hole. No one got the $20,000 but memorable shots were plentiful with Gary Tremblay chipping in the long 7th hole for a birdie and Charles Bazzard’s chip violently striking the flagpole before dropping into the chip. The KP was won by Ann McLeod after 8 years of male dominance.

entries.title: James Sinclair
entries.description: James starts working at Maracaibo. James had done a few jobs at Maracaibo working as part of Eddy Jang’s contractor crew. A man of many talents we were happy to have James as a full time employee by the end of 2000.

entries.title: Bird Count
entries.description: John and Noreen Davies took part in the annual bird count. They reported seeing 234 birds at Maracaibo – 32 different species. These would have included ducks. (Photo – Osprey)

entries.title: Carol Singing and Hay Ride
entries.description: We had a record turnout for Carol singing and Hay ride on Christmas Eve. The trailer, complete with lights, music and a canopy, was filled to capacity. The ride home was a little bumpy as the trailer blew a tire but luckily there were two tires on each side so no problem!

entries.title: New Strata Property Act
entries.description: The new act required Maracaibo to revise the Strata Bylaws and rules to conform. Luckily our lawyer at McCarthy Tetrault had chaired the committee charged with developing the new Act, so we had the very best advice. Charles joined the membership of the Strata Agents of BC and the Condominium Home Owners Association and attended several meetings to help prepare for conforming with the new Strata Property Act

entries.title: Maracaibo Web Site
entries.description: An old school friend of Charles, who visited at Christmas, offered to create a web site for Maracaibo at no charge. He lived in Indonesia, the programming was done in India and the site hosted in New York. Charles had to learn the skills required especially for the cottage booking system. It was relatively early days in web site management and we had to learn code to make changes and updates to the site.

entries.title: Land Management
entries.description: Plan approved for selective tree removal in District Lot 8 and other areas. Forestry proposal Feb 2001 – letter to Directors

entries.title: Investments Review
entries.description: The market value of our portfolio for the year ended 31/12/2000 produced a return of 11.43% The investment balance stands at $671,527

entries.title: Cottage improvements
entries.description: Balsam and Cedar Cottages were given a makeover – gyproc added to ceilings and a portion of the walls. With new lighting and furnishings this made a big diffence to the feeling inside the cottages.

entries.title: Islands Trust
entries.description: Community zoning plan finally approved, Maracaibo’s development plans are supported under the new zoning. After attending many many meetings we are happy to see progress. Charles participated as a member of the environmental committee of the Islands Trust.

entries.title: 5 Ton Truck
entries.description: Maracaibo purchased a 1950’s five ton truck that had previously been used to clear snow from Nanaimo airport. The cost of the truck was around $2,000 complete with hefty snowplough. A few years later at the Harry Potter Olympics the truck became the engine of Hogwarts Express. Still in use we have had our moneys worth out of this vehicle!

entries.title: Replacing lagoonl sluice gate
entries.description: The outer sluice gate installed in 1964s, finally rusted through. To control the water level in the lagoon a new gate needed to be installed at low tide. Using the workboat to transport a generator and arc welder to the site the old hinge was cut free and a spare gate installed. In the picture James Sinclair and Sam Anderson

entries.title: Core Area powerlines
entries.description: Quote from newsletter #97. “For many years Members have been saying it would be really wonderful if the powerlines across the meadows in the Core Area could be buried…..The Directors would like to hear Members views.” In November the Directors decided that burying the power lines in the Core Area should be postponed until the infrastructure for the compact housing development is underway.

entries.title: Swimming Lagoon Major cleanup
entries.description: We had an unusually high weed growth in the Lagoon in May. With a dry June we were able to do a good job of removing the mud. Over 100 truck loads were taken out and new sand spread on the beach.

entries.title: Land Management – logging
entries.description: Selective logging on a portion of District Lot 8 completed. Our logging contractor Mike Pierce from Nanoose Bay has single handed done an amazing job and cleanup. 17 logging truck loads were harvested from lot 8.

entries.title: Land Management Lot 8 cleanup
entries.description: Work continues on road restoration, trail development, broom removal and digging ponds

entries.title: Neighbour Hood Watch and Earthquake Preparedness
entries.description: More than 60 members attended a meeting in the barn organised by the Galloways and zone captains. Chuck Hamilton was the guest speaker. In 2001 the zone captains were: Zone 1 -Bazzards. Zone 2 Glen Champion and John Wellman, Zone 3 Galloways and John Pickering, Zone 4 Rupert Hooper and Gundy McLeod, Zone 5 Harvey Wright and Glen Whitelaw. Maracaibo becomes more prepared to respond to emergency situations with fire equipment and training.

entries.title: Logging Core Area and Adjacent Lots
entries.description: Logging moves to the Core Area, east and west of the works yard, and on some adjoining strata lots. Also around the tennis court, where a new trail is created. To empty the lagoon as much as possible we require very low tides. We blocked the intake pipe and ran two pumps continually to overcome the seepage at high tide. It took a week!

entries.title: Olympics 2001
entries.description: 2001 Space Oddysey – following the success of Aussie Olympics we decided to have a theme for the event and it proved a great success.

entries.title: Olympics weather
entries.description: Sundays weather deteriorated and we had to hurriedly move the BBQ from the meadow to the barn and rig up tarpaulins so the events and dinner could continue. We announced that because of the rain the Balloon Toss would have to be cancelled, but the participants were having none of that and the event continued regardless!

entries.title: Killer Whales in Longharbour
entries.description: The whales don’t often venture far into the harbour but in 2001 they were seen west of the ferry terminal.

entries.title: Round Prevost Race and End of Summer Potluck
entries.description: The Decision was made to sail around Prevost Island the wrong way. We did not know it was the wrong way until the end of the race when strong currents in Captains Passage prevented the fleet from returning to Longharbour. The leaders were held in the current allowing the rest of the fleet to catch up. In the end Bryan Williams in O’Desdirata was first accross the line. Kirk and Helen Robinson attended the BBQ and were recognised as the founders of the Round Prevost race in their boat Fortune Cookie. Early day challengers included Eric and Helen Jeanes in their boat Dolphin Striker.

Quote from Newsletter #100 “The events of September 11 2001 with planes destroying the World Trade Centre and damaging the Pentagon have undoubtedly affected us all. Our hope is that out of this terrible deed the world will emerge as a better place with greater understanding between people, religions and nations. At times like these we are very thankful to live in a place like Salt Spring Island.”

entries.title: Bazzards 25 years – Holiday
entries.description: The Bazzards are given a bonus in the form of a Mexican holiday as appreciation of their 25 years working at Maracaibo. In the photo they are heading to Isla Marietas in the Bay of Banderas. As you can see from the grins in the photo they had a wonderful time.

entries.title: Newsletter #100
entries.description: The first Newsletter was dated October 1981 and replaced the memorandums from John Lansdell and Quentin Brown.

entries.title: Surveys
entries.description: Surveys on the Fisherman’s Island and Compact Housing in the Core Area were sent to Members.

entries.title: Alarm System Monitoring
entries.description: The Managers will no longer monitor alarm systems in Maracaibo. FXR will take over the majority of the systems installed by Charles over the years. Monitoring the systems has caused many a sleepless night, as alarms could be triggered by spiders in the sensors and various other malfunctions as well as a very few genuine incidents. The Directors felt the managers should no longer be exposed to the dangers of encountering a burglar, as had previously occurred.

entries.title: Compact Housing Survey
entries.description: 17 Members expressed an interest in purchasing within 3 – 5 years, and 18 more within 5-10 years. As a result preliminary planning will proceed.

entries.title: Fisherman’s Island Survey
entries.description: The overwhelming number of Members favoured option 3b which was to incorporate the Island into the Strata Development when it became available for purchase. It was noted this is likely the hardest option to achieve.

entries.title: Land stewardship – Trails
entries.description: Trails completed in the Core Area following the logging activity. New trails were built along the ridge overlooking the meadows, around the tennis court and down towards the pickleball court plus each side of the worksyard.

entries.title: Shake or Shingle Roofs
entries.description: The Strata Council proposes the following change to the Guidelines on roofs in the Strata Development. There has been much debate on this subject and the fire risk associated with cedar shakes or shingles has become widely accepted as a reason to seek alternative roofing material. (roofs pdf) ROOFS

entries.title: Bridge Night
entries.description: Bridge continues to be played in the Members Lounge on a Monday night. Don Longley was the organiser

entries.title: Fire Equipment
entries.description: Maracaibo’s arsenal of fire fighting equipment is expanded. Increasingly dry summers and fears of forest fires keeps us on high alert in the summer. From June through September the 1 ton truck is fitted out with a water tank, pump and equipment ready to go. A group of Member volunteers attends regular fire practices led by Keith Galloway.

entries.title: Investment Income
entries.description: Due to the recession precipitated by 9/11 Investment income is expected to be $10,000 below budget. As a result capital spending is scaled back.

entries.title: Compact Housing / Cluster Housing
entries.description: The Directors received a report from the committee and accepted their recommendation to change the project name to Cluster Housing. Bob Hassell and Charles Bazzard staked out possible housing sites, access routes and septic field areas. The Directors were concerned about impacts on the meadows and decided to spend time considering alternative siting options. Marketing options included a lease option but we were advised not to proceed with that scenario. Bob Hassell, Gerard Farry, Leslie DeAthe and Charles Bazzard were asked to prepare a Master Plan for the whole of the Core Area.

entries.title: Staff
entries.description: Gwyn Gardam is back working at Maracaibo for her third summer. Gwyn is working wonders with the landscaping at Maracaibo and helping organise the Olympics. Photo of Maracaibo staff 2001. Left to right – Sally Bazzard, James Sinclair, Charles Bazzard, Eddy Jang (part time), Gwyn Gardam, Anno Delaney.

entries.title: Harry Potter Olympics
entries.description: Quite a different Olympics for 2002 as we enter the magical world of Harry Potter. Teams were sorted by the Sorting Hat. Gwyn Gardam our summer helper was the inspiration behind the program. Graham Clay was Dumbledore, Lindsay Mundy was Mrs. McGonagall, James was Hagrid and Charles was Hedwig. We had several Harry Potters, Hermione’s and Weasleys. Not sure if we had a Malfoy but Lord Voldemort was there. The ceremony started with children entering through the wall at platform 9 and 3/4 They then climbed aboard Hogwarts Express for a ride to the lake. Boats were then boarded to cross the lake and arrive at Hogwarts for the sorting ceremony. Sunday afternoon several games of quidditch were played and enjoyed. Lynne Cooper suggested the Harry Potter theme and for several years helped with the planning and organizing of the Olympic themes.

entries.title: Watering Restrictions
entries.description: In the middle of August Maracaibo asked residents to restrict water use for the first time. The summer had been extremely dry and we needed to ensure the wells were not overtaxed.

entries.title: Golf Tournament
entries.description: 18 hole Champions were – Gary Tremblay, Gary Brady, Peter Mc Hardy and Ann McLeod and the 9 hole champions were – Don Reimer, Maureen Rowell, John Wellman and Laurel Gordon. KP winner was Peter Rowell who was also MC for the event as Gundy was suffering from a broken rib.

entries.title: Birds Nest Fire
entries.description: A fire started in a birds nest built in a wooden outdoor light fitting at a home at Maracaibo. Luckily the fire was spotted and the Fire Department put the blaze out with minimal damage to the house. However the event highlit a number of concerns about fire risk and the ability of a firetruck to access a house site up a typical long windy tree lined Maracaibo driveway. As a result Members were encouraged to improve their access driveways.

entries.title: Round Prevost Race and End of summer BBQ
entries.description: Winner by handicap was Greg Slakov who sailed a laser around Prevost. Richard Fleck in Mistral was first over the line. After the BBQ – 50 Lanterns made from milk cartons were launched into the pool creating a magical affect as they glided gracefully around. Thanks to Donna Reimer for that idea. (photos – Greg rounding Nose Point and the Captain’s meeting.)

entries.title: Insurance Rates Double!
entries.description: Insurance cost increases took us by surprise in 2002 increasing by 110.25%. We had no prior warning of this increase, until a couple of months before our policy renewal in June. The main reason for the increase was a result of 9/11 which resulted in insurance losses of $50-75 billion US.

entries.title: Core Area Planning Study
entries.description: A detailed study of the Core Area and its development potential was circulated to Members. During January and February information meetings were held on Salt Spring and in Vancouver to discuss the planning study. (pdf link) Planning Study Lot 72

entries.title: New name for the Core Area
entries.description: Members are asked for suggestions for a new name for the Core area. 24 families submitted suggestions. After considerable debate no consensus on a name change was agreed and the name remains unchanged. Amongst the suggestions were “the Meadows” and “Corazon”.

entries.title: E-Mail
entries.description: Newsletter # 111 noted that approximately 50% of Members now have e-Mail

entries.title: AGM 2003 Cluster Housing
entries.description: “The Members of Maracaibo Estates Ltd. support the concept of residential housing in the Core Area along the lines indicated in the Planning Study Highlights, Strata Lot 72, circulated to Members in January 2003.” There was considerable debate about what “along the lines” meant. The motion was put to a vote as a special resolution and was defeated with 63.2% in favour and 36.8% against. (note a 2/3rd majority was required tp approve the motion) The Directors were asked to prepare a specific recommendation for the Members to consider.

entries.title: Easter Egg Hunt
entries.description: Lots of Members at Maracaibo and 46 children 12 and under participated in the Easter Egg Hunt. Maracaibo is definitely in a peak grandchildren era!

entries.title: Cluster Housing
entries.description: The Directors held a retreat to discuss development in the Core Area. Major outcomes were 1. Seniors Housing would not be considered for future study. 2. Leasing the land would not be considered as an option for future study. 3.Options to consider phasing land subdivision and or home construction would be considered.

entries.title: Pioneer Olympics
entries.description: Lots of fun was had celebrating the pioneers who had previouly owned the Maracaibo property. 1887 John Norton – Portuguese. 1891 Mahons – Irish. 1922 Abbott – English. 1934 Baldwin – USA. 1947 Mouat Cdn / Scottish. 1957 Charles Moat English.

entries.title: Coffee Mornings
entries.description: Coffee mornings continue to be very popular events. The Williams hosted in August and the morning was further enhanced by a performance by harpist Cassandra Miller. Casandra is a Canadian experimental composer currently based in London, England. In 2003 she was the choral Director for Tuned Air on Salt Spring.

entries.title: Valdy Concert
entries.description: A Maracaibo first, a concert in the meadow. The Wiggans and Wettsteins kindly donated a Valdy concert that they had purchased at the ArtSpring auction. Members enjoyed a lovely evening bringing their own picnics and a wonderful outdoor concert in the meadows. Valdy proved why he is such a succesful performer, not just a folk singer but a great entertainer who delighted young and old alike. A few members thought they were coming to a performance of Vivaldi, but they were happily delighted too!

entries.title: Golf
entries.description: The 13th annual tournament was a great success with 60 golfers participating. Winners – 18 holes were:- Gary Brady, Bob Quart, Don Quart, and Linda Tremblay. Winners of the 9 holes were the Charlton family:- Jim, Wendy, Sam and Troy

entries.title: Extreme Fire Risk
entries.description: The Summer of 2003 was hot and dry, wonderful for holidays, but fire hazard was extreme for an extended period. Water levels reached all time lows and Members were asked to conserve water. Big fires in the interior prompted us to issue an evacuation preparedness alert. Maracaibo will be obtaining a new book about FireSmart practices to circulate to homeowners.

entries.title: Round Prevost Race – Eddy Jang Retirement
entries.description: No one finished the Round Prevost Race, due to lack of wind. Eddy Jang was guest at the End of Summer BBQ and he was officially thanked for his many years of working at Maracaibo. By the end of 2002 Eddy Jang officially retired after almost 40 years of working at Maracaibo either as a contractor or part time employee, having started in the mid 1960’s building the A frame cottages for Charles and Mary Moat. It is interesting to note that a gift for Eddy from the Members was to be used for a trip to China, but the trip was on hold because of the pandemic caused by Sars.

entries.title: Broom Removal
entries.description: Members efforts at broom removal are recognised by BC Hydro. We are given a one time grant of $15,000 towards broom removal. A team of cutters is hired to help with the removal job. District Lot 10 is almost 100% clear of broom!

entries.title: Snow
entries.description: A heavy snowfall. Luckily we had bought a second hand snow plough for Hogwarts Express recently. It was the plough that had originally been used on our truck when it ploughed the Bamberton cement plant roads. James was in his element driving Hogwarts, and with Charles driving the 1 Ton truck with snow plough in tandem, we were able to keep ahead of the snow build up! Following the freezup there were 5 water leaks, including a burst irrigation line that had not been drained and a broken pipe in a house that caused considerable damage.

entries.title: High Speed Internet
entries.description: High Speed Internet has not reached Maracaibo yet and dial up through the phone system is very slow and frustrating. Doug Chapman and Gary Brady organise information and a survey to see if high speed internet can be delivered to Maracaibo.

entries.title: Property Assessments
entries.description: 20% was the norm for property assessment increases for Salt Spring.

entries.title: Canadian Army
entries.description: A training exercise for troops heading to Afganistan was held on Salt Spring. The exercise included Mansell Road with some troops in disguise. Members were warned that there may be suspicious looking characters in the vicinity.

entries.title: AGM & Cluster Housing Survey Results
entries.description: The Cluster Housing survey results indicated that there were not sufficient Members interested in actually living in a home in the Core Area. As the purpose of development was to meet Members needs rather than their investment objectives it was decided not to proceed with any further planning. It was noted that unless there is a hot topic for discussion at an AGM they can be boring! The Managers noted that they were happy not to have any hot issues under debate!

entries.title: Bear
entries.description: There was great excitement in June when Willie Rycroft (Airedale dog) chased a bear up on to the Tremblay’s lot 86. The bear was seen again shortly after by the Farrys on their property and then, also by the Farrys, on Jo Ann Martin’s driveway! The animal control officer assured us that this was a healthy young male bear with no criminal record – in fact, he was less trouble than the average tourist – so he was quite unconcerned. Residents were relieved however when the bear was reported as being down in the Fulford area again. Bear sightings are very unusual on Salt Spring. This one must have swum across from Vancouver Island. (Bear in photo taken by Charles but not at Maracaibo)

entries.title: FireSmart
entries.description: Don Reimer helps organise Members to carry out tree thinning and FireSmart limbing to reduce fire risk on the property

entries.title: Pancake Breakfast
entries.description: Celebrating Canada Day – approximately 140 Members and families attended the breakfast. Latecomers found all the food had gone!

entries.title: Extreme Fire Risk
entries.description: By July we were warning of extreme fire hazard having been notified that the potential for a major forest fire on Vancouver Island had reached a 400 year high! Maracaibo increases its supply of fire fighting equipment which includes a supply of Barricade foam. (photo Keith Galloway demonstrating with a blow torch how an area of plywood treated with Barricade foam does not burn.

entries.title: Chipper
entries.description: Maracaibo purchased a wood chipper to help deal with branches collected from FireSmart work

entries.title: Greek Olympics
entries.description: Celebrating the return of the real Olympics to Athens. it was fun to turn the spotlight on our own Maracaibo family with Greek ancestry, the Acuros family. Nick Acuros was delighted to light our 5 Olympic rings. It had been our intention to keep things simple, but somehow, once everyone’s ideas had been incorporated, we had quite a spectacular opening ceremony. Doug Chapman and Gary Tremblay offered to make us a chariot, then with the help of James and Henry and Charlie Winstanley, we ended up with four. Each chariot was beautifully decorated by team captains, The Beckmanns led the parade with their Trojan horse (golf cart) full of pint-sized soldiers, and 16 members of the Rowell family raised banners made by Maureen, Maryann Wiggan and Shelagh Brady. A new event was the Maracathalon, which involved running in full armour, driving a chariot pulled by 3 ‘slaves’, archery, discus throwing, carrying an olive, and then swimming to the finish! Joyce Sharpe organised Greek dancing, and a group of women practiced several times over the summer. Not to be outdone several men tutored by Leslie DeAthe performed their version of Greek dancing to the delight of all.

entries.title: Building Guidelines and FireSmart
entries.description: The Guidelines were updated to reflect changes to building materials and allow more flexibility for homeowners to meet the goals of FireSmart.

entries.title: Pancake Breakfast
entries.description: After organising this event for several years Gundy Mcleod handed over the reigns. Gary Brady, and several others carried on the tradition. Gundy was presented with a BBQ apron by Lynne Cooper. ( Photo Gary on the left Gundy on the right.)

entries.title: Speeding
entries.description: Following several complaints, the Strata Council agreed to review speeding and road safety for the next AGM.

entries.title: BCTC – BC Hydro Transmission Lines
entries.description: BC Hydro hold a public information meeting re their proposed increase of transmission cables to serve Vancouver Island. The Transmission lines will run through the existing Hydro easement at Maracaibo, but the change will result in more towers and potentialy increased EMF. Subsequently a number of Members donated funds to a local group organised to appeal the proposal and prepare alternate suggestions. Charles participated in the group and over the next two years was involved in a number of meetings and appeared at the BCTC hearing as an intervenor on behalf of Maracaibo Estates Ltd. At the end of the proceedings BC Hydro was allowed to proceed, but a number of conditions had to be met and BC Hydro cooperated in removing broom at Maracibo, digging some ponds and creating some firebreak trails on the edges of the Transmission line easement. (photo shows old and new towers – the number of towers doubled but BC Hydro considered them more pleasing to look at!

entries.title: Easter Egg Hunt
entries.description: The Wiggan family provided 18 bunnies to help hide eggs, almost as many as the children looking for them!

entries.title: Tennis Tournament
entries.description: There were less players than usual. Harry White and Dawn Montgomery were the winners. The roast lamb dinner at the Main House proved as popular as ever.

entries.title: Team Maracaibo – Run for the Cure –Canadian Breast Cancer Foundation
entries.description: Diane, Hillary & Eric Rudd, Nicki, JC and Haley Horton, Tish, William and Duncan Kenny, Jeff, Sarah, Michael & Morgan Omstead, Heather Brekke, Valerie Hayes, Laurie Stewart, Linda Tremblay, Sally Rycroft, and Sally Bazzard all ran for the cure in Vancouver. Becky Bazzard was one of the organisers. Many members were financial sponsors.

entries.title: Pirate Olympics
entries.description: The pirate theme for the Maracaibo Olympics was great for our location, close to 400 attended the BBQ on Sunday evening our young pirates in full costume were treated to a trip around Clamshell Island by the captains and crews of Kittiwake (Boudins), Hilda Grace (Somervilles), Tillicum (Truscotts) and Eaglemar (Kenny’s & Vogels). For the opening ceremony, the pirates sailed across the lagoon to pick up their crews and then with blood curdling yells they raced forward and captured the Maracaibo Directors in the Fort (built by the power-pole) at the edge of the lagoon. A ransom was demanded which was for the promise from the Directors to investigate the burying of the powerline that crosses the meadow and lagoon. The Directors agreed on the condition that the Long John Charles walk the plank! Everyone and especially James and Toby really enjoyed Charles being forced to walk the plank in shark infested waters.

entries.title: Martini Night
entries.description: Martini Madness at the barn organised by George Pitman and Bob Quart for the August Happy Hour truly gave meaning to the name!

entries.title: Round Prevost Race
entries.description: The 2005 race was one of the best; there was wind for the start, and a good variety of weather conditions during the race. 9 boats started, and for the first time in several years they all finished. First across the finish line was Tillicum (Truscotts), followed by O Desiderata (Williams), and in third place Karalan (Shrives). First on Handicap was Gulf Odyssey (McLennans)

entries.title: Golf
entries.description: Gundy McLeod, having done a wonderful job of Organising the Golf Tournament that he started in 1991, steps back and Ken Austin and Glen Champion step forward to organise the event. (photo Gundy left Ken Right.) Gundy McLeod Trophy. This is a new trophy to be awarded each year as the organizing committee sees fit. This year the winner was obvious. It was presented to Gundy, in honour of his hard work over the years in putting on this tournament. The trophy depicts a young Scot swinging a golf club.

entries.title: Lot 8 Meadow
entries.description: Following the clearing work in October, we have had an area of 3 + acres in the centre of District lot 8 ploughed in preparation for seeding and rolling in the spring. The soil is excellent, and we hope to create an attractive open space that we can keep mowed. This will be a good area to allow dogs and children to run, and best of all, it will be easy to keep the broom under control. If this is successful, we hope to expand the area.

entries.title: BC Hydro Land Stewardship Recognition
entries.description: In recognition of Maracaibo’s Land Stewardship Plan and efforts to remove broom BC Hydro donated 20 hours of broom mowing. They dug a new pond west of the Trincomali substation, and the existing pond by the road leading to the substation was partially re-opened. A firebreak was cut down to the Trincomali Trail along the existing but overgrown trail close to the Lot 12/13 boundary and then looping back and coming out by Lot 9. This has opened another walking trail. A firebreak was mowed at the west end of the Trincomali Trail, following the existing overgrown trail and alongside the powerline easement. The pond, about 100 metres west of Rainforest Road, was partially widened and deepened. A large flat area west of the pond was mowed, so that we can keep it mowed in the future. A new trail was developed along the south boundary of District lot 8.

entries.title: BCTC Transmission Lines
entries.description: Maracaibo registers as an Intervener in the BCUC hearings. Charles attends numerous meetings and several hearings in Vancouver. The end result was BC Hydro had their way, but the Utility Commission felt that sufficient good arguments were put forward that BC Hydro had to pay their legal costs and BC Hydro had to purchase a number of homes in Tsawwassen that would be negatively affected.

entries.title: Core Area Power Lines
entries.description: Having survived walking the plank at the Pirate Olympics – Charles prepared a plan of how the power lines could be buried in the Core Area. (15 years later it happened!)

entries.title: Strata Corporation Management
entries.description: New legislation effective January 1st, 2006 requires strata management companies be registered as brokers and that individual managers become licensed. Effective January 1st the Strata Corporation will no longer be managed by Maracaibo Estates Ltd. Charles and Sally will become employees of the Strata Corporation as resident managers as well as being employed by Maracaibo Estates Ltd as managers. The Strata Council will make decisions regarding the management of its assets and contract out services accordingly.
