Maracaibo Estates will be contracted to operate the water system, carry out road maintenance and maintain the common land. The only noticeable change for members will be that they must pay their strata fees directly to Strata Corporation 905.

entries.title: No hayride……..
entries.description: The Christmas Eve hayride tradition had to be ended as we felt that the risks are too great at this time of the year. The event is so popular and the load on the trailer heavy. The tractor brakes are not good at the best of times and coming down the hill to the Core Area was alarming last year!

entries.title: Insurance
entries.description: Our facilities were inspected for liability concerns and as a result a number of improvements have now been completed. The playground has been reconstructed to conform to the latest CSA standards. James has done a super job of rebuilding it. The deck railings at Clamshell Cottage have been replaced to conform to the building code. Unfortunately its built-in bench had to go. The hearth on the fireplace at Dogwood has been extended and several other minor items attended to. Our insurance premiums for 2005 decreased and the savings were diverted to pay for the upgrades.

entries.title: John Lansdell
entries.description: John died on March 27th. John was the principal partner in a real estate development and holding conglomerate that consisted of Griffith Lee and Wilson, Marlowe Yeoman and Gulf Pacific Investments Ltd. From an earlier connection with John Lees while working for the Yorkshire Trust (Mary Moats brother), John Lansdell and Quentin Brown became friends with Charles and Mary. When the Moats decided to sell their property, they approached John and Quentin and it was then that the concept of Maracaibo was first conceived. John, a lawyer by training, was a master at putting together syndicates of investors and that is how Maracaibo as we know it began. You can read more about the early days in the book “The Magic of Maracaibo.

entries.title: Combined AGM
entries.description: For the first time the meetings of Maracaibo Estates Ltd and Strata Corporation 905 were combined. This resulted in a better flowing meeting. Article changes approved at the meeting were subject to policies being reviewed to ensure members are fully informed about unbudgeted expenditures being made and that the Members would be given the opportunity to vote on those expenditures.

entries.title: Directors Elections
entries.description: Following the AGM Doug Chapman was elected as President of Maracaibo Estates Ltd and Chairman of the Strata Corporation. Doug and Leslie Deathe (a future President) had built a home on Seclusion Lane. After several years of commuting to Toronto Doug became a full time resident and fully involved in Maracaibo affairs. Dr Graham Clay remained on the board for another year. Doug remained as Chairman until his term was completed in 2012

entries.title: Core Area powerline burial postponed
entries.description: It was agreed that the cost is too high in relation to the net benefit. Even after having been forced to walk the plank at last years Olympics, Charles agreed it was hard to justify the cost of relocating the lines at the present time.

entries.title: Speed Detector
entries.description: To help monitor the ongoing speeding problem on Nose Point Road a speed monitor was purchased and used to record and display vehicle speeds. There was a definite improvement as drivers became more aware due to the flashing red lights!

entries.title: Pancake Breakfast & Fire Preparedness
entries.description: From humble beginnings for a dozen or so residents at the Gazebo this has grown to a big event – there were well over 120 people for breakfast at the barn. The breakfast was followed by a presentation from the SSI Fire Chief on FireSmart, a program designed to reduce the risk of wildfire spreading and to encourage protection around your homes. The presentation was very well received with about 100 in attendance. The presentation ended abruptly as the Fire Chief left the meeting to attend an emergency with sirens blazing. That certainly got everyone’s attention.

entries.title: BCTC- Powerline Transmission
entries.description: In July, the BC Utilities Commission granted approval for the BC Transmission Company to build a new AC line to Vancouver Island to replace the existing AC lines. The new lines will transmit many more times the amount of power presently transmitted. The approval was granted on the premise that the BCTC option was the lowest cost application. The Utilities Commission did not consider that the impacts of aesthetics, property values, health impacts etc. were of any significant consequence!

entries.title: Land Stewardship
entries.description: Peter Sharpe arranged for a botanist to walk the Nose Point area with himself, Chris Galloway, John Heddle and Charles. She was looking at the qualities of the area as a Garry Oak environment and was delighted to find several native grasses and plants that are only associated with a Garry Oak area. We hope to identify wildflowers and learn how best to protect them from deer browsing and other damage.

entries.title: Coffee Parties
entries.description: Hosts were the Jessimans and Wrights

entries.title: Fire Risk
entries.description: The extended dry period made us concerned about a forest fire, especially after watching the water bombers picking up water in Trincomali Channel to fight the fire on Galiano Island. We had fire practices and our 1-ton truck loaded with fire equipment on standby.

entries.title: Cablevision & High Speed Internet
entries.description: Shaw Cable purchased Salt Spring Island Cablevision on July 1st. Maracaibo will get high speed internet via the cable system, and a much greater choice of TV channels.

entries.title: Narnia Olympics
entries.description: The opening ceremony with Mr. and Mrs. Beaver, involved the arrival of the Ice Queen in her Chariot accompanied by a “Little” dwarf and Father Christmas. Aslan was introduced with a great roar! Can you imagine snow at Maracaibo in August? Only at the Narnia Olympics! (We hope!). We transformed a portion of the barn into the winter forest where children and the young at heart met the Ice Queen, Mr. Tumnus, Miss Fox, and Father Christmas. After sampling Turkish Delight and being granted a wish, the children passed through another door to reach summer at Narnia. Here they played games and made crafts.

entries.title: Narnia Olympics
entries.description: George Pitman and Bob Quart organised another Martini night for the August Happy Hour.

entries.title: Shari Ulrich Concert
entries.description: Alan Wiggan organised a Concert by Shari Ulrich in the meadow; proceeds went to the Lady Minto Hospital. It looked as though Shari was enjoying playing in the wonderful setting of Maracaibo as much as we enjoyed listening to her. Paul Omstead entertained us with a couple of songs in the interval and prompted requests for another concert incorporating more Maracaibo talent.

entries.title: Tennis and Pickelball
entries.description: The games courts were re surfaced.

entries.title: House destroyed by fire at Maracaibo
entries.description: Richard Clarke and Andria Scanlan’s brand new home was completely destroyed by fire in the early morning of Sept 6th just a couple of weeks before they were due to move in. Due to the extremely high fire risk, there was high probability of the fire spreading to the surrounding forest. Fortunately, the vegetation in the direction in which the fire was spreading had been thinned, and low branches removed following the FireSmart principles. This undoubtedly made it much easier to access the area to put out spot fires. The Salt Spring Island Fire Department responded fast and did an excellent job. Glenn and Sally Rycroft, neighbours, raised the alarm and started to fight the fire. Glenn, one of the Maracaibo fire fighting volunteers knew how to get the fire hose ready to go from the nearby firebox. He was soon joined by Keith Galloway and Charles Bazzard with the Maracaibo fire fighting equipment. Many Members, their families and friends helped fighting the fire, putting out spot fires, phoning the community, night watch at the site, walking the powerline and property looking for spot fires, conserving water.

entries.title: Golf
entries.description: 37 players had a great day golfing. Glen Champion organised the event. 18 Hole winners were Earle and Jackie Morris and Colin and Heather Lawler. Nine-hole winners were Peter and Maureen Rowell and Jim and Fran McLennan.

entries.title: Land Stewardship
entries.description: As a continuation of work started last fall, we have now cleared about 5 acres of land at the west end of the transmission line right of way in district lot 8. The rocks have been removed, the ground ploughed, tilled, seeded, fertilized, and rolled so we expect to see fist signs of grass growing by the end of October. This is the first stage of a three-year plan to create an extensive meadow along the right of way in lot 8 wherever the terrain permits. The main purposes for doing this work are to develop a large mowable firebreak on our south west boundary, an area that was very heavily infested by broom. Additional benefits will be aesthetic and a great place to let a dog run, hit a golf ball etc.

entries.title: Land Stewardship
entries.description: The grass planted in the meadow in lot 8 sprouted beautifully

entries.title: Carol Singing
entries.description: This annual event is now held in the barn.

entries.title: Flying Car
entries.description: A car did not make the corner on Nose Point Road before the bend leading down to the Kingfisher Lane turnoff. The car flew off the road and almost made it to Kingfisher Lane. Amazingly no one was hurt.

entries.title: Snow
entries.description: 2006/2007 was quite a winter; someone said there have been 15 major windstorms, plus the snow!

entries.title: Special General Meeting Strata 905
entries.description: As a follow up to the housefire on Seclusion Lane, strategies were presented and approved by the strata lot owners to improve our ability to respond to and reduce the risk of fires at Maracaibo. Notice of a Special General Meeting final

entries.title: Internet access
entries.description: Internet access for Members is made available in the Members Lounge. Finally, the dialup modem is gone!

entries.title: Main House in the 1920’s
entries.description: Cousins Ashley Prinables of Australia and Elaine Osterberg of Burnaby came to see where their fathers, Dick and Tom Abbott, spent part of their childhood during which the main house was built (1922-33). They brought us copies of several interesting old photos including this one.

entries.title: Easter Egg Hunt
entries.description: It was great to celebrate the return of spring and to welcome back our Maracaibo families amid the flowers and blossoms and all those chocolate eggs. We all gathered by the main house for drinks and cookies and the rain held off just long enough for us to enjoy it!

entries.title: AGM
entries.description: We had a good turnout for the combined AGM which included several resolutions of a housekeeping nature. Following the meeting over 60 members stayed to enjoy an excellent buffet dinner at the Harbour House Hotel.

entries.title: Fire Protection
entries.description: Considerable progress had been made with the FireSmart initiatives approved in February, including work along the beaches and trails, purchasing of equipment for 5 new fire boxes. In addition Maracaibo has purchased a truck for use as a dedicated fire fighting vehicle. It is equipped and ready for service.

entries.title: Tennis
entries.description: The 2007 Maracaibo Mixed Tennis Tournament was smaller than usual. Eight players thoroughly enjoyed the camaraderie and ‘three sets each’ format. Carolyn Mouat and Ernst Kramer had a perfect score 18 to win the trophy. The day was rounded out with a very pleasant meal together at a local restaurant.

entries.title: Broom Removal
entries.description: Thanks to a dedicated group of broom pullers, great inroads have been made in removing broom from the east end of the Transmission line, Clamshell to Islet Beach, the Nose Point Area, and several sections of the roads. Many lot owners have also been busy clearing their lots of broom as well as the adjoining common land. This is a huge community effort that will benefit the property for years to come.

entries.title: Canada Pancake Breakfast
entries.description: Over 100 attended the breakfast – again organised by Gary Brady and his team.

entries.title: Roofs
entries.description: After years of debate the policy on roofing material at Maracaibo was revised. “Roofs should be sloped wherever possible. Due to increasing concern about fire risks, priority must be given to the fire resistance of roofing materials. Fire resistant roofing materials that simulate cedar shakes or shingles in profile and colour are preferred options. Other options may be approved if they have an exposure, profile and colour tone that the Strata Council deems acceptable.”

entries.title: Coffee Mornings
entries.description: Jane Hickie and Michele Dunkerley, Nick and Marge LeMoine, and Murray & Beth Feller all hosted coffee

entries.title: Bullock Lake Resort Fire
entries.description: Excerpt from Times Colonist article. “SALTSPRING ISLAND — Local citizens who took to the dark forests of Salt Spring Island with flashlights, shovels and water are being credited with preventing the Salt Spring Island Village Resort fire from growing out of control and threatening nearby houses. Around 15 people from a strata development called Maracaibo Estates traveled more than two kilometers to battle spot fires with backpacks full of firefighting foam and water Monday night. Assistant fire chief Arjuna George said strong winds spread fire embers “the size of hockey pucks” more than a kilometer away, sparking more than 100 spot fires. “It was raining burning embers,” said Charles Bazzard, Maracaibo Estates strata general manager, who was one of the volunteer citizen firefighters.” Fire fighters – Carla Rhodes, James Sinclair, Charles Bazzard, Keith Galloway, Glen Rycroft, Abe Hohn, Greg Slakov, Gary Brady, Gary Tremblay, John & Barb Wellman, Mike Overholt, Dan Smith, Willy Bartel, Alan Wiggan, Bob Quart; (not able to get through – Toby Stubbs, David, and Bob Niven). Back up team – Louise Quart, Frank and Lynne Cooper, John and Claire Pickering, Sally Bazzard, Chris Galloway, Shelagh Brady, Selise Brady Lebedovich, Linda Tremblay, Liz Smith and Jennifer Bartel.

entries.title: BC Hydro
entries.description: BC Hydro were unable to access their substation with large transporters and required an access easement across common land. The Strata Owners received $26,900 from BC Hydro in compensation. The funds will be placed in the road replacement reserve.

entries.title: Circus Olympics
entries.description: Olympics – We wondered where we would go with this theme but thanks to great input from our staff and Members it all came together – we even had an eleven foot elephant for our parade.

entries.title: Creativity in the Core
entries.description: A new community event hosted by Beth Feller and Claire Pickering. Wednesday afternoons at 2 pm – come and bring your paints, pencils, knitting, quilting needlework project to the Gazebo to share talents just for fun.

entries.title: Martinis and Steak
entries.description: The Pitmans and Quarts expanded their martini night and, with the help of Gary Brady and Mike Overholt, served up steak dinners to about 61 people. The Bradys won the ‘door’ prize of 4 dinners.

entries.title: Transmission Lines
entries.description: BC Hydro has now started construction of the new transmission line.

entries.title: Easter Egg Hunt
entries.description: A beautiful sunny Easter weekend

entries.title: AGM
entries.description: Planning committee explained scope of asset replacement and maintenance and other issues to be faced over the next 15 years. Members were asked to comment on the development of 16 lots in District lot 8. Revisions to the Articles and Policies were approved.Planning Presentation 2008

entries.title: Spring at Maracaibo
entries.description: Excerpt from Newsletter #139 – Finally some spring weather and what better place to enjoy it than Maracaibo! Sally and I went to look for the spring wildflowers that we find in various places that are not usually browsed by the deer. Our first stop was the cliff face south east of Secret Beach, here we found Indian Paint Brush and a little further along patches of Sea Blush and Blue-Eyed Mary and lots of Stonecrop. A single quail made a great show of getting our attention. As we walked along, we found some Coral Root and Calypso Orchids. Out of the trees along the shoreline the grasses neatly trimmed by the deer were a fresh bright green. Then we came across a gully in the rocks right on the shoreline full of brilliant dark blue Camas next to burgundy coloured moss; quite spectacular. As we approached Candlestick Cove, we came within 30 ft of an immature eagle perched on a low branch of a Garry Oak right over the trail. On our way back we hiked to the bench overlooking Trincomali Channel and watched two porpoises feeding just off the shore. We felt so lucky to have all this at our doorstep.

entries.title: Tennis
entries.description: The 2008 Mixed Tennis Tournament held on a fine day in May was a great success. There were 16 participants; the men outnumbered the women this year. Everyone enjoyed the days play on those excellent courts. The tennis was friendly yet competitive. Harvey Wright and Martin Hope won the event with Elisabeth Tielens and John Peters as runners up. The day concluded with a very enjoyable dinner and prize-giving at the barn.

entries.title: Broom Removal (Report from Chris Galloway)
entries.description: “This year has been such a rewarding year for broom pulling/cutting. The daisies and foxglove have once again claimed their land rights along the hydro line and what a show they have given us to enjoy! We may never win the war on broom but we have proved broom can be managed well in the following areas: Along the hydro line west of the Trincomali Sub Station to the north of Clamshell, Big Bluff and area, Willows Pond and Nose Point. We also tackled the roadside this year from Clamshell to the south of the entrance to Trincomali Sub Station. Charles and his crew have addressed the roadway east of the mailboxes and the brush cutter will do the rest. I would like to thank the following volunteers for helping to manage the broom: Glen Rycroft, John Pickering, Michael Oliver, John Heddle, Keith Galloway, Greg Slakov, Chris Baker, Sue Baker, Katie Baker and friend, Adam Baker and friend, Linda Tremblay, Alan Wiggan, Maryann Wiggan, Sally Rycroft, Brian Keir, Ann Keir, Peter Sharpe, Joyce Sharpe, Rae Jessiman, Charles, James, Toby and Danielle. Very special thanks to Joyce Sharpe and Judy Heddle for their wonderful baking. Also thank you to everyone for looking after their own lots. Hope everyone can join us next year!”

entries.title: Speeding
entries.description: Every year reminders are needed to ask drivers to slow down on our narrow windy roads.

entries.title: Canada Day Breakfast
entries.description: Gary Brady co-ordinated the pancake breakfast again this year. The sun shone, breakfast was great, the pancakes extra fluffy (thanks Toby) and as usual it was a great start to our summer season with the singing of “O Canada”.

entries.title: Coffee Parties
entries.description: Were hosted by Janet Stethem, and Doug Chapman and Leslie DeAthe, member living outside Maracaibo. Both homes were designed by Hank Schubart who also designed many of the homes at Maracaibo. Coffee parties have proved a great way for members to meet and a wonderful opportunity to see Members’ homes whether in Maracaibo or elsewhere on Salt Spring Island.

entries.title: A Taste of the Orient Olympics
entries.description: While not perhaps quite as spectacular as the Beijing version, we were proud of how our Oriental theme came together. The barn was transformed by our staff into an oriental market, the costumes of participants were great, our team captains proved to be excellent drummers as well as leaders, and Angela, Julie, Rosie and Frances were amazing under Carol’s wonderful lion dance mask and train, and Toby excelled himself as our DJ for the dancing.

entries.title: Special General Meeting
entries.description: The Directors held a special meeting on August 18th to ask shareholders to approve a proposal to spend funds to allow the company to proceed with the exploration of water sources sufficient to service a sixteen-lot development in the Remainder of District Lot 8 and to prepare a preliminary layout plan showing the proposed roads and lots. The proposal will be to pay these expenses by using the proceeds from the issue of two new Maracaibo share packages, although because of timing issues, the expenses may be paid from the Contingency and Development Fund on an interim basis. Motions were passed to spend up to $95,000 on planning a development of District lot 8 and proving adequate water supply. Also approved was the issue of two new shares from Maracaibo treasury to fund the expense.

entries.title: Lot 8 Development
entries.description: Two wells were drilled in District Lot 8 in September and formal draw down tests were carried out on each of the wells. We were very lucky to find two good wells. The first came in at about 5 gallons per minute after continuous pumping for 3 + days and the second well came in at approximately 15 gpm. This means that we have proved sufficient water supply to meet the subdivision requirements for a community water system.

entries.title: Golf
entries.description: The 2008 Invitational Maracaibo Golf Tournament was organised by Gary Brady 28 participants included Maracaibo Members and their families. The 9 hole “Maracaibo Scramble” format brought out the best in all the players. Throughout the afternoon the word “FORE!” could be heard. After the golf, a delicious buffet of hot and cold appetizers was served to all the players at the Falcon Head Grill. This year’s championship team trophy for the best ‘low net’ score went to Keith Austin and Alison, Mike, and Mathew Baskerville-Bridges. Keith Austin also won the men’s longest drive on the 8th hole. The lady’s longest drive was won by Linda Tremblay.

entries.title: Cottage Gift Certificates
entries.description: The idea of Maracaibo gift certificate for cottage bookings was introduced in time for Christmas presents.

entries.title: World Financial Crisis
entries.description: The world economic situation set the tone of our Directors / Council meetings on the 10th of October 2008, influencing a focus on keeping expenses down and postponing spending on capital improvements and replacements where possible until the present financial crisis turns around.

entries.title: BC Hydro
entries.description: Work at the cable terminal is still ongoing but at a much slower rate. BC Hydro now have 24-hour security living on site following an incident where someone coming in by boat tried to cut and steal some the cable for scrap metal value, not realizing the cable was live. They were lucky to live. Hydro divers found a hacksaw in the sea. We presume the security will be there until the construction project is complete.

entries.title: Seclusion Lane Hockey
entries.description: An impromptu game of street hockey was held at the east end of Seclusion Lane.

entries.title: Master Plan for Development – District Lot 8
entries.description: Maracaibo Estates Ltd engaged Garyali Architect Inc (architects) to propose a Master Plan for Development specific to development plan options for the Remainder of District Lot 8. To achieve an understanding of the owners and families at Maracaibo and their visions for Maracaibo the architects requested a participatory design process involving a cross section of stakeholders (focus group) consisting of two workshops. A second focus group meeting was held, and the architects presented development concepts for the Remainder of District Lot 8. These were well received. Other things under discussion were upgrades to the Main House and replacing our 29-year-old backhoe Sustainable Development Planning

entries.title: Easter
entries.description: Despite a very rainy weekend we had a record turnout of children 12 and under for the Easter Egg Hunt. Lots of fun was had by all. We squished into the barn together after the hunt for coffee, hot chocolate and cookies.

entries.title: Tennis
entries.description: The 2009 Maracaibo Mixed Tennis Tournament held on a fine day in May was another success. Maracaibo staff had worked hard on court maintenance and it was much appreciated by the players. There were 16 participants; the play was friendly yet competitive: Maracaibo residents always enjoy the visiting members from Vancouver. The tournament was won by Van Oldenborgh and Lynne Cooper with runners up, Kevin Elwood and Diana Kramer. A very enjoyable dinner and prize-giving was held in the Main House in the evening. Special congratulations to Lynne Cooper- after all the years of organizing!

entries.title: Coffee Party
entries.description: Dick and Patty Vogel hosted a coffee party at their new home on Mariners Lane.

entries.title: Pancake Breakfast
entries.description: Gary Brady organised the event “This year’s Canada Day pancake breakfast was held on July 4th under warm sunny skies. Over 130 were in attendance including kids of all ages, parents and grandparents. Once again, our chefs; Alan Wiggan, Bob Quart, Harvey Wright, John Pickering and Mike Overholt demonstrated their outstanding skills at the BBQ’s. In addition, the “pancake griddle king” and head chef George Pitman turned out five star cuisine with the assistance of our new “batter boy” Brian Keir. Special thanks to Marilyn Pitman, Gary & Linda Tremblay, Nick LeMoine, Charles & Sally Bazzard and Shelagh Brady for their help and assistance.”

entries.title: Golf
entries.description: Gary Brady ran another excellent event. Fifty-six competitive and highly spirited golfers turned out to put their name on the coveted “Maracaibo Championship Trophy”. The championship foursome was the team of Sue & Chris Baker, Eileen & Tom Connolly. Other trophy winners were: Ladies and Men’s Longest Drive- Joan Winstanley and Richard Clarke. KP on the par 3 number 2 hole for men and women combined was Rae Jessiman. Gary Tremblay won KP for the men.

entries.title: New Shares Issued
entries.description: Two new shares were issued from treasury and sold to Members on the waiting list. The proceeds of the sale of these shares is used to reimburse the Contingency and Development funds that had been used for planning and water drilling expenses in District lot 8.

entries.title: Summer 2009
entries.description: A very hot summer, Long Harbour was so warm that many Members swam in the harbour rather than the swimming lagoon!

entries.title: Medieval Olympics
entries.description: Decorating the barn as a castle was a total team effort due to the colourful and innovative shields that families had created. Max Manley (Beckmann) played trumpet to announce the parade and Angus Graeme led playing his bagpipes. The costumes were highly creative, with knights, damsels, an executioner, drummers, Robin Hood, wizards and witches, horses; and Charles, as Monty Python, looking for the Holy Grail and losing control of a parade! A combination of the noise of the bagpipes and Charles shouting instructions inside his helmet meant no one in the parade could hear him. Chaos ensued as the parade marched on past the King following the piper while Charles pranced about on his horse trying to get them to stop. It was all a lot of fun. King James opened the games after knighting our team captains. The activities at the castle were a great success and the volunteers seemed to be having as much fun as the children. We were delighted with the popularity of the sandcastle competition, a new event that will be repeated. #147 Olympics Photos

entries.title: Round Prevost Sailboat Race & End of Summer potluck.
entries.description: The sailboat race was scratched due to a poor weather. The End of Summer Potluck was a happy gathering of stalwarts who braved the elements and enjoyed a fun get together in the shelter of the barn. With the propane heaters going it was quite cosy!

entries.title: Asset Replacement Presentations
entries.description: The Board of Directors prepared a detailed preliminary plan on how to address our major asset replacements over the next fifteen years. A presentation of the plan was held in Vancouver on December the 7th and another on Salt Spring Island on December the 9th. Feedback from the presentations has resulted in some fine tuning of the recommendations.

entries.title: Yukon Quest
entries.description: In February 19 yr old Peter Fleck and a team of 14 sled dogs completed the Yukon Quest, a two-week race between Fairbanks and Whitehorse. His father, Richard Fleck, drove the expedition’s support vehicle. The 1,600-kilometre (1,000-mile) race runs along frozen rivers, crosses over a 1,200-metre (4,000-foot) snow-shrouded peak and passes through some of the country’s most scenic and unforgiving wilderness. It was also winter, which means Peter and the 23 other racers did most of their racing in the dark.

entries.title: Winter storms in Long Harbour
entries.description: We had a few anxious days because of storms this winter. As well as bringing down trees and subsequent power outages, the first winds broke loose a boat that was being renovated at anchor out towards the ferry dock. This fifty+-footer was washed onto the beach by the Easter Meadow where it sunk. Three cats were rescued from the boat, and Charles spent a couple of nights at low tide helping the search and rescue team to see if the holes in the boat could be plugged. We were much relieved when the owners finally had it removed by a tug using a couple of large pumps to keep it afloat. A few weeks later another large motorboat came loose from its mooring near our dock and collided with a catamaran that was swept to the extreme end of the inlet. The big boat then became entangled with a small sailboat. We towed it to our dock once the weather died down to keep it from further mischief and it is now safely back on a new mooring buoy – a hard lesson in the need to check anchor chains!

entries.title: Easter
entries.description: Our annual Easter Egg Hunt was very well attended as usual. The children really enjoy it and so do the adults. It was a wild and stormy weekend, but the rain held off on Sunday. It was fun to meet again over drinks and cookies on this first community event of 2010.

entries.title: AGM
entries.description: This was a more complicated AGM than usual with several resolutions, all of which were passed. The resolutions were associated with approval of the implementation of Maracaibo’s asset replacements and also included amendments to the Company Articles and Authorised share capital. 1. Asset Management and Land Management Plan

entries.title: Marketing
entries.description: Alan Wiggan and Gary Brady develop a strategy to enhance the marketability and profile of Maracaibo and begin the process of updating the Maracaibo website.

entries.title: Tennis
entries.description: “Twenty players enjoyed a sunny Saturday on May 15th when for the first time we had two 14-year old’s and two 17-year old’s, one of whom, Torben Roberston, won the tournament with partner, Virginia Campbell. Runners up were Elly Fontein and Paul Beckmann. Dinner in the Main House was catered by Christine and 29 folks were entertained by Kevin Elwood who had us singing Land of Hope and Glory as well as reading out limericks. He then recited the very humorous story of Albert and the Lion in memory of Harvey Wright who has told it to us on past occasions. John Pickering won the night by reciting The Return of Albert, which had us all laughing out loud! Even the teenagers said, “this is much more fun than our parties”!

entries.title: House / Office / Lounge (HOL)
entries.description: Doug Chapman, Claire Pickering and Charles Bazzard, with the experienced help of Max and Alannah Malin, will be responsible for guiding the process of the Main House replacement and making recommendations to the Board. Letters requesting expressions of interest have been sent to a short list of 5 architects/designers and we hope to start the design process as soon as possible. Built in 1922 and expanded in 1928 the house built on cedar logs laying on midden and is subject to flooding at extreme high tides. After considering options to raise and renovate the house on a proper foundation it was deemed simpler and more cost effective to remove the old house and rebuild.

entries.title: Mushrooms
entries.description: Zoe Clarke with some huge mushrooms found near Rain Forest Road. “Agaricus Augustus” (“The Prince”). They can grow up to 17 inches in diameter and are safe to eat. If you find edible mushrooms and want to harvest some, be sure to leave a few so that they will regenerate. Sometimes it takes years before mushrooms will return to the same area as conditions have to be perfect for mushrooms to grow. Be very careful though. Many mushrooms are poisonous and tricky to identify.

entries.title: Fire Practice
entries.description: We held a full-scale fire practice on the 15th of June in conjunction with the Salt Spring Island Fire Department. It was a great opportunity to try the phone tree, calling out volunteers and advising residents of the practice. 25 volunteers from the SSI Fire Department, 13 Maracaibo members and staff were actively involved in the exercise as well as phoners. We were able to see how we could integrate our equipment and volunteers to help in an emergency situation. It was a positive learning experience for everyone.

entries.title: Broom Removal
entries.description: Chris Galloway thanked participations in this year in organized broom cuts. This year focused on the hydro line between Trincomali Sub Station and the Slakovs home, Big Bluff / Clamshell/ Willows Pond and the roadway.

entries.title: Dock Safety
entries.description: We have installed several white ladders on the docks to help those who fall in get back out again. We have also placed several life rings with throwing lines. Remember if you must throw a ring hold onto the end of the line!

entries.title: Coffee Mornings
entries.description: Thank you to the Pickerings who hosted a coffee pary on July 10 and the Acuros’s on the 24th.

entries.title: Canadian Summer Olympics
entries.description: Our theme was to celebrate the winter Olympics that had been held in Vancouver. The torch relay was reinstated and over 150 participants, from toddlers to 80-yr old’s, carried James’s homemade torch from Nose Point, past cheering onlookers, spurred on by Toby and his megaphone, to our Inukchuk at the firepit. JC Horton (Erickson) in full costume lit our Olympic “flame” with the actual torch he had carried in February. Bill Cooper shared his wonderful collection of Olympics memorabilia including three real torches from Turin, Beijing, and Vancouver.

entries.title: Lobsters and Oysters
entries.description: As an extension of the Martini madness event Bob Quart and George Pitman arranged for a wonderful seafood dinner at the barn. Fresh oysters and lobsters were flown in from Nova Scotia!

entries.title: Golf
entries.description: “The 2010 Maracaibo Open Golf Tournament was held at the SSI Golf & Country Club under warm sunny skies. The 9-hole event was attended by 56 golfers that included Maracaibo members and their guests. The champion chip trophy was awarded to the foursome of Marge and Nick LeMoine and Maureen and Peter Rowell. The ladies’ and men’s longest drive trophies went to Maureen Rowell and Al Wiggan. On hole #2 Jane Hickie won the ladies trophy for KP ‘closest to the pin’ while Earl Morriss won the Ian Jessiman trophy for the combined KP for men and women. Special recognition was given to Gundy and Ann McLeod for organizing our tournament for 14 years beginning in 1991. Since they will be leaving Maracaibo, we will surely miss them and wish them the very best.”

entries.title: Broom Removal – BC Hydro
entries.description: BC Hydro will be cutting target trees and broom in the late spring/ early summer of 2011. This will be a huge boost to our volunteer broom cutters and it is in large part due to their efforts that we have been able to persuade BC Hydro to assist in clearing the broom from the transmission line right of way.

entries.title: Main House Replacement Siting
entries.description: Rob Barnard has been hired to obtain approvals and plans for the replacement of the Main House. A site survey has been undertaken and in the New Year an archaeology report will completed. A geo-technical survey will also be carried out in January. There are a number of challenges associated with building on the existing site including acquiring a variance from the Islands Trust to build on the partial footprint of the old house but at a raised elevation. Photo shows archaeological test holes to locate midden areas. Impact assessment June 3 2011

entries.title: Main House Replacement
entries.description: Work continues on the planning for the main house replacement. Preliminary archaeological work has been completed as well as survey, geotechnical and site planning. A development permit application is before the Islands Trust. If all goes well, we should have some schematic plans to present later this summer.

entries.title: New Website – New Logo
entries.description: Alan Wiggan introduced our new web site live at the annual general meeting and explained the changes that had been made to make the delivery of information more accessible. Gary Brady explained the marketing benefits. A meeting was held to introduce the new web site to the local real estate agents. Twenty-two agents attended for a presentation and lunch, and we now have links on our web site directly to properties that are listed for sale at Maracaibo. Many thanks to Alan and Gary who spearheaded the effort to revitalize the design of our website and to make it easier for prospective purchasers to access information about Maracaibo.

entries.title: Facebook
entries.description: Maracaibo Facebook site designed and set up by Becky Bazzard. There is a direct link to it from the Members section of the our website or you can connect directly here. The site is accessible to everyone and you do not have to join Facebook to view the site.

entries.title: Easter
entries.description: The Easter Egg hunt was very well attended with about 50 participants and lots of parents and grandparents looking on. This is always a very popular community event with many of us reconnecting after the winter months.

entries.title: Summer Staff accomodation
entries.description: After housing and feeding summer staff (about 100 of them) for 35 years Charles and Sally give the summer a miss as they prepare to move to their new home. The summer staff stayed in a cottage until needed by members and then move to a tent and boat! (Giselle and Erika).

entries.title: New 4 wheel drive JCB Backhoe
entries.description: After 30 years of good service the 1980 Case Backhoe was sold to James and a new 4 wheel drive JCB Backhoe purchased.

entries.title: Broom
entries.description: Broom removal has been an outstanding success this year. We have never seen the area of the transmission line right-of-way between lots 6 and 16 look better. Very many thanks to Chris and Keith for organizing again this year and to all who remove broom on their own properties, those who keep the power line free of broom adjacent to their properties and those who remove broom when out on walks such as in the Nose Point area. The power line walk was quite spectacular during June with so many wildflowers in bloom. The masses of daisies, foxgloves, rose campions, wild roses and ocean spray were amazing. Another huge boost this year has been BC Hydro’s transmission line management work. In addition to removing danger trees, they agreed to mow down the broom wherever accessible in recognition of our community efforts to remove broom and our assistance in mowing the access roads and meadow in lot 8.

entries.title: Pancake Breakfast
entries.description: Many thanks to Gary Brady and his group of trusty volunteers for putting on another great Pancake Breakfast.

entries.title: Amaryllis
entries.description: Long time resident sailboat at the dock Amaryllis belonging to Bob Hassell and Masayo Hora is given a major overhaul culminating in a party at the Gazebo following a large group effort of friends who helped carry the main mast down to the dock so it could be taken round to Ganges for installation later by crane.

entries.title: Nautical Nonsense Olympics
entries.description: This was a fun theme for Maracaibo. It was good to utilise our wonderful natural amenities and talents to the full, from Gary Tremblay’s and the children’s’ beautiful little sailboats, to the best laser race in years. Marilyn Pitman and friends put so much effort into the barn activities and Tom Sadlier has transformed the running races for children from a somewhat stressful competition to a major fun highlight as the kids warm up for their big race!

entries.title: Room at the dock
entries.description: John Vogel came over in his 62 ft sailboat “Hold Fast”. She is the largest sailboat we have seen at the dock, and draws to much to stay when the tides are low!

entries.title: Hall Of Fame
entries.description: Congratulations to Audrey Williams on being inducted into the BC Sports Hall of Fame for her contributions to figure skating! “Vancouver’s Audrey Williams stands as one of the all-time great skating officials from BC.” International Judge, ISU Referee, Olympics team leader for female skaters, mentored dozens of individuals who rose to prominent roles, served on provincial and national committees ranging from skater development to official development to judging.

entries.title: Fire Practice
entries.description: Thanks to Keith Galloway for helping organise a joint practice with our Maracaibo volunteers and the Salt Spring Island Fire Department. The SSI fire department were very happy to have the practice and complimentary about our volunteers and equipment. We took our fire truck along the trail to Wreck Beach (not accessible by the SSI fire trucks). Then we practiced relaying water from the fire department’s trucks to our truck. We also set up a sprinkler system as a protection barrier and several Maracaibo volunteers stood by with backpacks and shovels ready to attack spot fires. We also practiced fighting a fire from our workboat with a fire pump on board, and then shuttled water to our fire truck to expand our water capacity. It was a great exercise and a good learning opportunity.

entries.title: Golf Tournament
entries.description: Gary Brady organised another successful tournament “On August 13th under warm sunny skies 56 golfers played in the 2011 “Maracaibo Invitational Open Golf Tournament”. Tom Connolly and Chris Baker demonstrated the latest in men’s golf attire. The championship trophy was awarded to the team of Paul Beckmann, Stephen Bartley, Edward Bartley and Michael Oliver. The ladies’ and men’s longest drive went to Allison Little and Al Wiggan. On hole #2 Andrew Stewart won KP, closest to the pin, for the men while Audrey Williams won the Ian Jessiman trophy for the combined KP for men and women.

entries.title: Canada in the 2012 Olympics.
entries.description: Member – Richard Clarke is actively racing in a Star class sailboat hoping to qualify to represent Canada in the 2012 Olympics.

entries.title: Coffee Morning
entries.description: Michael Oliver and Lorna Gail Proudfoot opened their new home at 136 Fisherman’s Lane to us all and served us coffee and treats. They have done an amazing job with the house and the sunny courtyard. This wonderful display of wildflowers is maintained by emitters on the septic field. Thank you very much for a most enjoyable morning.

entries.title: Class C Shares
entries.description: The Board of Directors approved the issue of the shares at a Special Meeting on September 12th. Key highlights are, $1 million offering, $1,000 per share (minimum purchase 5 shares), Annual fixed, cumulative, preferential cash dividend. The dividend rate for the first year will be 4.84%. In subsequent years the rate will be reset annually at a rate equal to the average of the 5-year Government of Canada bond yield for each of the preceding 12 months plus 2.5%. All outstanding Shares must be redeemed by the Company in 2019. The purpose of the share issue was to raise capital to finance the replacement of the Main House.

entries.title: HOL – Main House Progress
entries.description: The Islands Trust approved our Development Permit Application to rebuild on the same site at a higher elevation. Rob Barnard is the designer and project manager. The building contract was put out to sealed bid and was awarded to Derek Sowden, of Strait Construction Ltd. Asset Management and Land Management Plans

entries.title: Managers Retirement Plans
entries.description: Charles and Sally will be retiring 31 December 2012. Replacement managers will be hired to overlap with Charles and Sally for November and December 2012. Charles and Sally will be hired as management consultants through 2013 on an as needed basis.

entries.title: Office Relocated
entries.description: In October, the office moved to Cedar Cottage, in preparation of demolishing the Main House. Internet service was connected to Cedar Cottage and wireless internet access to Arbutus, Balsam, and the barn areas. The Bazzards moved to their new home on Seclusion Lane. Improvements were made to the barn, creating a TV area using old doors from the Main House, as compensation for loss of the Members Lounge. Photo – the dark office in the Main House, originally the dining room.

entries.title: Class C Shares
entries.description: the one million dollar offering was fully subscribed within a few days, this allows for the financing of the New House Office and Lounge (HOL)

entries.title: Preparation for Main House Demolition
entries.description: Insulation containing arsenic is removed from the attic of the Main House.

entries.title: Maracaibo Calendar
entries.description: Maracaibo sells “2012 Maracaibo Calendar” and promotes them as Christmas presents for $20 each.

entries.title: Storms
entries.description: “We have had a continual procession of wet and stormy days and nights. We had the strongest southeaster we have seen, with waves breaking over the seawall along the meadow edge! Lots of fallen trees, some damage to the dock and a couple of days without power, but by and large we fared well.”

entries.title: Main House demolition
entries.description: The old house is down – the photo shows the old living room fireplace and the three cedar logs that were the foundation of the original part of the house.

entries.title: Easter
entries.description: Another good crowd for the egg hunt

entries.title: New Managers hired
entries.description: Pete and Victoria Davidson were hired in April and will have a two month overlap with Charles and Sally starting in November.

entries.title: President
entries.description: Alan Wiggan is elected as President of Maracaibo Estates Ltd and Chairman of Strata Corporation 905. Alan played a major roll in developing and implementing the Asset Management Plan. This included replacing the Main House, Development of 9 bare land strata lots in the Core Area and the transition of the Managers.

entries.title: Round Salt Spring Race
entries.description: Richard Clarke (Seclusion Lane resident) and Tyler Bjorn have teamed up to pursue an Olympic medal in the Star Class sailing event at the London 2012 Olympic Games. Greg Slakov, Mike Pickering, and Charles Bazzard had an amazing day sailing on the Round Salt Spring Race with Richard. Richard had been lent the “Braveheart” a 52ft Transpac sailboat. There was a crew of 16 including several seasoned sailors. It was a thrill to be on such a finely tuned boat and even better to be first over the line at the start and finish! Greg Slakov is suspended between the sails up the mast looking for wind!

entries.title: Office
entries.description: The office is moved from Cedar Cottage to a trailer at the top of the meadows.

entries.title: House Fire
entries.description: A house fire on Strata Lot 3 resulted in a total loss. the response from the SSI Fire Department, ambulance service and RCMP was much appreciated. Maracaibo volunteers were terrific, with Greg Slakov, Keith Galloway, Glen Rycroft, Chris Baker and Adam & friend and James all attending and helping at the scene. Many thanks also to Andria Scanlan, Beck Bazzard, Sally Bazzard, Sue Baker, Chris Baker and Chris Galloway, who all helped with phone calls, answering questions. A very special thank you to Cinda Helm, who did not hesitate to make her home available to Gus and Rob as well to everyone who provided meals wine and other essentials to keep them going.

entries.title: Pancake Breakfast
entries.description: The breakfast was held at the barn on Saturday June 30th. The event was well attended, breakfast was delicious and a great time was had by all. Many thanks to Gary Brady and his group of trusty volunteers for putting on another great Pancake Breakfast.

entries.title: Main House Archaelogical
entries.description: The majority of the Main House was built on top of an old midden. Extensive archaeological work was required to satisfy ministry and First Nation requirements. In the end only a few fragments of fish bones were found.

entries.title: HOL Foundations

entries.description: On the morning of December 20, just before the first tree blocked Mansell Rd. Well beach and Nose point as well as in Lot 8.Fortunatly there was very little damage to any of the homes in Maracaibo. “The Dec 20 windstorm caused more damage and required the largest mobilization of resources than any previous storm in its history ” – BC Hydro Calm before the storm The WIliam’s driveway Nose Point Rd. entries.title: Covid 19
entries.description: Maracaibo in 2020: A Year That Shifted Everything In early March 2020, we sent out a regular newsletter celebrating Maracaibo’s 50th anniversary, sharing updates on cottage rentals and ongoing community business. Within days, everything changed. As the Covid‑19 pandemic advanced, operations across the island—and around the world—came to an abrupt halt. Immediate Impacts Cottage bookings were cancelled almost overnight. Members already staying in cottages chose to extend their stays as travel restrictions tightened. Board meetings moved to Zoom and were held every couple of weeks to keep pace with the rapidly evolving situation. Keeping Maracaibo Running Despite the uncertainty, Maracaibo staff were able to continue working, ensuring essential operations remained stable. Projects already underway moved forward, though supply delays became a regular challenge. Welcoming Guests Back—Carefully By summer, we were able to welcome Canadian members and guests back to the cottages under strict Covid protocols. Stays were shortened to allow for additional cleaning and distancing. Sadly, our international members were unable to travel and were deeply missed. Staying Connected Community connection took on new forms: A few virtual happy hours on Zoom brought familiar faces together during the spring. Summer happy hours shifted outdoors to the meadow, with a fully BYOE approach—bring your own everything.
